learn: Equal rights mean that every person deserves the same basic respect, fairness, and opportunities, regardless of gender, background, ability, or beliefs.
Promoting equal rights involves treating everyone fairly, standing against discrimination, and including people who may be left out or treated differently.
Respecting the rights of others means listening to different perspectives, avoiding judgment based on differences, and treating people the way you would want to be treated.
A community that values equal rights becomes more peaceful, fair, and supportive for everyone who lives in it.

lessons.title: I Am Humble
lessons.sub: Defining Humility, Humility as a Sign of Faith, Ways to Show Humility
learn: Humility means having a modest view of one's own importance — not boasting about achievements and recognizing that everyone has strengths and weaknesses.
Humility is often connected to faith, as many teachings encourage being humble before God and treating others with equal respect regardless of status.
Ways to show humility include admitting mistakes, giving credit to others, listening more than talking about yourself, and avoiding bragging about achievements.
A humble person is often more respected by others because humility shows genuine character, kindness, and openness to learning from others.

lessons.title: I Value Cleanliness
lessons.sub: Maintaining Cleanliness, Collaborative Efforts, Hygiene and Waste Management
learn: Maintaining cleanliness at home and in school involves regularly tidying spaces, properly disposing of trash, and keeping shared areas neat for everyone.
Cleanliness is a collaborative effort — it works best when everyone in a family or classroom takes responsibility for keeping their shared spaces clean.
Good hygiene practices include regular handwashing, bathing, and brushing teeth, which help prevent the spread of germs and illness.
Proper waste management, such as segregating trash and recycling, is an important cleanliness-related measure that protects both health and the environment.

chapters.title: F. I Play Traditional Filipino Games with Other Children

lessons.title: I Play Traditional Filipino Games with Other Children
lessons.sub: Types and Cultural Significance of Traditional Filipino Games
learn: Traditional Filipino games include patintero, luksong tinik, piko, sipa, and tumbang preso — games often played outdoors with simple materials.
These games are usually played in groups, which helps children build teamwork, cooperation, and social skills while having fun.
Traditional Filipino games carry cultural significance because they have been passed down through generations and reflect Filipino community values like camaraderie and creativity.
Playing these games helps preserve Filipino heritage and gives children an active, screen-free way to bond with friends and family.

gmrc.title: Community Resources as Cultivators of Good Habits

chapters.title: A. I Recognize the Contributions of Outstanding Persons with Disabilities

lessons.title: I Recognize the Contributions of Outstanding Persons with Disabilities
lessons.sub: Inspiring Filipino PWDs, Impact of Valuing PWDs, Advocating for Inclusion
learn: Many Filipino persons with disabilities (PWDs) have made outstanding contributions in sports, arts, and other fields, showing that disability does not limit a person's ability to achieve great things.
Valuing the contributions of PWDs positively impacts society by promoting acceptance, reducing stigma, and inspiring others to overcome their own challenges.
Advocating for inclusion means making sure PWDs have equal access to opportunities, spaces, and resources in schools, workplaces, and the community.
Simple ways to advocate for inclusion include treating PWDs with respect, avoiding discrimination, and helping create accessible spaces for everyone.

chapters.title: B. I Have a Family that Obeys the Rules and Regulations of My Community

lessons.title: I Have a Family that Obeys the Rules and Regulations of My Community
lessons.sub: Community Guidelines, Importance of Following Rules
learn: Communities set rules and regulations, such as curfews, waste disposal guidelines, and noise policies, to keep residents safe and maintain order.
Families that obey community rules help create a safer, more organized, and more peaceful environment for everyone who lives there.
Following community rules also sets a good example for children, teaching them the importance of respecting shared guidelines throughout their lives.
When rules are broken, it can lead to safety risks, conflicts among neighbors, or a breakdown of order within the community.

chapters.title: C. I Understand Good Leadership Qualities

lessons.title: I Understand Good Leadership Qualities
lessons.sub: Qualities of a Good Leader, Finding Future Leaders
learn: Good leaders often show qualities like honesty, responsibility, fairness, good communication, and the ability to listen to and inspire others.
A good leader considers the needs of the whole group, makes thoughtful decisions, and takes responsibility for both successes and mistakes.
Future leaders can be found and nurtured by giving children opportunities to lead small tasks, encouraging teamwork, and recognizing positive leadership behaviors early on.
Anyone can develop leadership qualities over time by practicing honesty, responsibility, and kindness in everyday situations.

chapters.title: D. I Am Honest and I Live with Integrity

lessons.title: I Am Honest and I Live with Integrity
lessons.sub: Recognizing Acts of Honesty, Building Relationships through Honesty
learn: Honesty means telling the truth and being sincere in your words and actions, even when it might be difficult or uncomfortable to do so.
Acts of honesty include admitting mistakes, returning something that isn't yours, and telling the truth even when no one is watching.
Integrity means consistently doing what is right, even when it's hard, and having your actions match your values and beliefs.
Honesty helps build strong, trusting relationships, because people feel safe and respected when they know they can rely on someone's word.

chapters.title: E. I Take Care of Animals

lessons.title: I Take Care of Animals
lessons.sub: Basic Needs of Animals, Human Impact, Promoting Animal Well-Being
learn: Animals have basic needs just like humans, including food, clean water, shelter, and proper care to stay healthy and safe.
Human actions, such as pollution, habitat destruction, and littering, can seriously harm animals and disrupt the balance of ecosystems.
Taking care of animals responsibly means providing for their needs, treating them gently, and never causing them unnecessary harm.
Promoting animal well-being can be done by supporting animal shelters, avoiding cruelty, and educating others about the importance of caring for animals.

chapters.title: F. I Value Historical Sites in the Community

lessons.title: I Value Historical Sites in the Community
lessons.sub: Exploring Historical Marvels, Promoting Historical Sites
learn: The Philippines has many historical sites, such as old churches, forts, monuments, and heritage towns, that reflect the country's rich history and culture.
Exploring historical marvels helps people understand the struggles, achievements, and traditions of those who came before them.
Valuing historical sites means visiting them respectfully, learning about their significance, and helping keep them clean and well-maintained.
Creative ways to promote historical sites include sharing their stories with others, joining community heritage events, and encouraging responsible tourism.

filipino.title: Kabanata I: Ako, Bilang Mabuting Tao

lessons.title: Panitikan – Kaya Ko!
learn: Ang kuwentong "Kaya Ko!" ay tungkol sa isang batang natututong magtiwala sa sarili at gumawa ng mga bagay nang mag-isa.
Ang katapangang subukan ang bagong bagay, kahit mahirap sa simula, ay isang mahalagang katangian ng isang mabuting tao.
Sa pagsasabing "Kaya ko!", ipinapakita ng isang bata ang positibong pananaw at determinasyon.
Ang pagtitiwala sa sarili ay lumalago kapag sinusubukan natin ang mga bagong hamon at natututo tayo mula sa ating mga pagkakamali.

lessons.title: Wika – Ang Pangungusap
learn: Ang pangungusap ay grupo ng mga salitang may kumpletong diwa o kahulugan.
Bawat pangungusap ay binubuo ng simuno (ang paksa o pinag-uusapan) at panaguri (ang sinasabi tungkol sa paksa).
Nagsisimula sa malaking titik ang unang salita ng pangungusap at nagtatapos ito sa tuldok, tandang pananong, o tandang padamdam.
Halimbawa: "Naglalaro ang mga bata sa parke." — dito, "ang mga bata" ang simuno at "naglalaro sa parke" ang panaguri.

lessons.title: Panitikan – Magkamukha pero Magkaiba!
learn: Ang kuwentong "Magkamukha pero Magkaiba!" ay nagpapakita na kahit magkatulad ang itsura ng dalawang bagay o tao, maaaring magkaiba sila sa loob o katangian.
Itinuturo ng kuwento na hindi dapat husgahan ang isang tao base lamang sa panlabas na anyo.
Bawat tao ay may sariling katangian, kakayahan, at personalidad kahit magkamukha sila ng iba.
Ang pagtanggap sa pagkakaiba ng bawat isa ay tanda ng paggalang at pag-unawa.

lessons.title: Retorika – Mga Pangungusap Ayon sa Gamit
learn: Ayon sa gamit, ang pangungusap ay maaaring pasalaysay (naglalahad ng ideya, nagtatapos sa tuldok), patanong (nagtatanong, nagtatapos sa tandang pananong), pautos (nag-uutos o humihiling), o padamdam (nagpapahayag ng matinding damdamin, nagtatapos sa tandang padamdam).
Halimbawa ng pasalaysay: "Maganda ang panahon ngayon."
Halimbawa ng patanong: "Saan ka pupunta?"
Halimbawa ng pautos: "Isara mo ang pinto." Halimbawa ng padamdam: "Ang ganda naman!"

lessons.title: Retorika: Mga Pangungusap Ayon sa Kayarian
learn: Ayon sa kayarian, ang pangungusap ay maaaring payak (may iisang simuno at panaguri), tambalan (dalawa o higit pang payak na pangungusap na pinagsama ng pangatnig tulad ng "at" o "ngunit"), hugnayan (may pangunahing sugnay at panalong sugnay na pinag-uugnay ng "kung," "dahil," o "nang"), o langkapan (kombinasyon ng tambalan at hugnayan).
Halimbawa ng payak: "Kumakain ang bata."
Halimbawa ng tambalan: "Kumakain ang bata at umiinom siya ng gatas."
Halimbawa ng hugnayan: "Kumain ang bata dahil gutom siya."

filipino.title: Kabanata II: Ako at ang Aking Pamilya

lessons.title: Panitikan – Kung Bakit Nagalit ang Pusa sa Daga
learn: Ang "Kung Bakit Nagalit ang Pusa sa Daga" ay isang halimbawa ng kuwentong pantasya na nagpapaliwanag kung bakit hinahabol ng pusa ang daga.
Ang ganitong uri ng kuwento ay tinatawag na kuwentong nagpapaliwanag ng pinagmulan ng isang bagay o pag-uugali.
Sa kuwento, may naganap na pangyayari na naging dahilan kung bakit nagkaroon ng alitan ang pusa at daga.
Itinuturo ng kuwento ang halaga ng katapatan at pagtupad sa pangako sa isa't isa.

lessons.title: Retorika - Ang Talata
learn: Ang talata ay grupo ng mga magkakaugnay na pangungusap na naglalahad ng isang pangunahing kaisipan o paksa.
Ang bawat talata ay may panimulang pangungusap (topic sentence) na naglalahad ng pangunahing ideya.
Sinusundan ito ng mga pangungusap na sumusuporta o nagpapaliwanag pa sa pangunahing ideya.
Ang talata ay nagtatapos ng pangwakas na pangungusap na bumubuod sa kaisipan.

lessons.title: Panitikan – Si Mariang Makiling
learn: Si Mariang Makiling ay isa sa mga pinakakilalang alamat sa Pilipinas, tungkol sa isang diwata na naninirahan sa Bundok Makiling sa Laguna.
Ayon sa alamat, tumutulong si Maria sa mga mahihirap at nangangailangan, ngunit nawawala siya kapag sinusubukang tingnan nang malapitan o sinusundan.
Ang alamat ay nagtuturo ng halaga ng kabaitan, pagbibigay, at paggalang sa kalikasan.
Ang Bundok Makiling ay itinuturing na sagrado dahil dito raw nananahan si Maria.

lessons.title: Retorika – Liham Pangkaibigan (Pagbati)
learn: Ang liham pangkaibigan ay sulat na ipinapadala sa isang malapit na kaibigan o kamag-anak upang makipag-usap nang impormal.
Ang liham na pambati ay isinusulat upang batiin ang isang tao sa isang natatanging okasyon tulad ng kaarawan o pagdiriwang.
Ang bahagi ng liham ay binubuo ng petsa, bating panimula, katawan ng liham, pagwawakas, at pangalan ng sumulat.
Dapat magaan at personal ang tono ng liham pangkaibigan, at makikita rito ang pagmamalasakit sa taong pinadalhan.

lessons.title: Retorika - Liham Pangkaibigan (Paanyaya)
learn: Ang liham paanyaya ay isinusulat upang anyayahan ang isang kaibigan o kamag-anak sa isang okasyon o kaganapan.
Dapat malinaw sa liham ang petsa, oras, at lugar ng kaganapan upang malaman ng inaanyayahan kung saan at kailan ito gaganapin.
Mahalagang magalang at malinaw ang paraan ng pag-anyaya upang agad maunawaan ng bumabasa ang layunin ng liham.
Katulad ng ibang liham pangkaibigan, may petsa, bating panimula, katawan, pagwawakas, at pangalan ng sumulat ang liham paanyaya.

filipino.title: Kabanata III: Ako at ang Aking Kapaligiran

lessons.title: Panitikan – May Ilaw na si Tap
learn: Ang kuwentong "May Ilaw na si Tap" ay tungkol sa isang tauhan na natutong maging kapaki-pakinabang sa pamamagitan ng pagbibigay-liwanag o tulong sa iba.
Sa kuwento, ipinapakita na ang bawat isa, gaano man kaliit, ay may kakayahang gumawa ng malaking pagbabago sa buhay ng iba.
Ang "ilaw" sa kuwento ay sumisimbolo sa pag-asa, kaalaman, o kabutihang ibinabahagi natin sa ating kapaligiran.
Itinuturo ng kuwento ang halaga ng pagiging mapagkalinga at mapagbigay sa kapwa at sa kalikasan.

lessons.title: Retorika – Sanaysay
learn: Ang sanaysay ay isang uri ng piyesang pampanitikan na naglalahad ng opinyon, pananaw, o karanasan ng sumulat tungkol sa isang paksa.
Ito ay binubuo ng panimula, gitna (katawan), at wakas na magkakaugnay sa isa't isa.
Maaaring personal, impormal, o pormal ang istilo ng pagsulat ng sanaysay depende sa layunin nito.
Ang mabuting sanaysay ay malinaw, organisado, at may malinaw na pananaw o mensahe na nais ipahatid sa mambabasa.

lessons.title: Panitikan – Ang Nagbagong Mundo
learn: Ang kuwentong "Ang Nagbagong Mundo" ay naglalarawan ng mga pagbabagong nagaganap sa kapaligiran dulot ng aksyon ng tao o kalikasan.
Itinuturo ng kuwento na may epekto ang ating mga gawain sa kalikasan, kaya't dapat tayong maging responsable sa pag-aalaga nito.
Ipinapakita rin sa kuwento kung paano nakakaapekto ang pagbabago sa kapaligiran sa buhay ng tao, hayop, at halaman.
Hinihikayat ng kuwento ang mga mambabasa na maging bahagi ng solusyon sa pag-aalaga ng ating planeta.

lessons.title: Retorika – Ang Anekdota
lessons.sub: Maikling Kuwento ng Tunay na Karanasan
learn: Ang anekdota ay maikling kuwento tungkol sa isang tunay na karanasan o pangyayari sa buhay ng isang tao.
Layunin ng anekdota na magbigay-aliw, magturo ng aral, o magbahagi ng masayang alaala sa mambabasa o tagapakinig.
Karaniwang maikli lamang ang anekdota at direkta sa punto, ngunit malinaw ang simula, gitna, at wakas nito.
Maaaring gamitin ang anekdota upang bigyang-diin ang isang aral o mensahe sa pamamagitan ng personal na karanasan.

lessons.title: Retorika – Pagsulat ng Anekdota
learn: Sa pagsulat ng anekdota, dapat piliin muna ang isang tunay na karanasan o pangyayari na nais ibahagi.
Isulat ang pangyayari ayon sa tamang pagkakasunod-sunod (simula, gitna, wakas) upang malinaw itong maunawaan.
Gumamit ng masining at buhay na paglalarawan upang maging kawili-wili ang kuwento sa mambabasa.
Tapusin ang anekdota nang may aral o mensaheng nais ipahatid mula sa naging karanasan.

filipino.title: Kabanata IV: Ako at ang Aking Lipunan

lessons.title: Panitikan – Ang Talambuhay ni Dr. Fe Del Mundo
learn: Si Dr. Fe del Mundo ay isang kilalang Pilipinang pediatrician na itinuturing na "Ina ng Pediatrics sa Pilipinas."
Siya ang unang babaeng naging estudyante sa Harvard Medical School noong 1936, bagama't hindi nila alam na babae siya nang tanggapin.
Nagtatag siya ng ospital para sa mga bata, ang Children's Medical Center, upang magbigay ng abot-kayang gamutan sa mga batang Pilipino.
Kinilala siya bilang National Scientist ng Pilipinas dahil sa kanyang malaking ambag sa larangan ng pediatrics at kalusugan ng mga bata.

lessons.title: Panitikan – Si Prinsipal Teroy
learn: Ang kuwentong "Si Prinsipal Teroy" ay tungkol sa isang mabuting pinuno ng paaralan na nagsisilbing modelo ng mabuting pamumuno.
Ipinapakita sa kuwento kung paano dapat pangalagaan at pamunuan ang isang paaralan o komunidad nang may pagmamahal at pananagutan.
Itinuturo ng kuwento ang halaga ng pakikinig, pag-unawa, at pagmamalasakit ng isang pinuno sa kanyang mga kasamahan.
Nagbibigay-diin din ang kuwento sa kahalagahan ng disiplina at respeto sa loob ng paaralan.

lessons.title: Retorika – Ang Talambuhay
lessons.sub: Buhay at Karanasan ng Isang Tao
learn: Ang talambuhay ay isang uri ng sulatin na naglalahad ng buhay, karanasan, at mga naging tagumpay ng isang tao.
Maaaring isulat ng ibang tao ang talambuhay ng isang tanyag na personalidad, o maaari ring isulat ng tao ang sariling buhay, na tinatawag namang awtobiyograpiya.
Karaniwang naglalaman ang talambuhay ng impormasyon tulad ng kapanganakan, pamilya, edukasyon, mga tagumpay, at ambag ng tao sa lipunan.
Sinusunod sa talambuhay ang pagkakasunod-sunod ng mga pangyayari sa buhay ng tao, mula pagkabata hanggang sa kasalukuyan.

lessons.title: Panitikan – Ang mga Itim na Sisiw
learn: Ang kuwentong "Ang mga Itim na Sisiw" ay nagpapakita ng aral tungkol sa pagtanggap sa pagkakaiba-iba ng bawat nilalang.
Sa kuwento, natutunan ng mga tauhan na ang kaibahan sa kulay o anyo ay hindi dapat maging dahilan ng pagtatakwil o panunukso.
Itinuturo ng kuwento ang halaga ng pagkakaisa at pakikitungo nang mabuti sa lahat, anuman ang kanilang pagkakaiba.
Nagbibigay-diin din ang kuwento sa kahalagahan ng pagmamahalan sa loob ng isang pamilya o pangkat.

lessons.title: Retorika – Pagsulat ng Talambuhay
learn: Sa pagsulat ng talambuhay, dapat mangalap muna ng sapat na impormasyon tungkol sa buhay ng taong isusulatan.
Ayusin ang mga impormasyon ayon sa pagkakasunod-sunod ng mga pangyayari, mula sa pinakaunang bahagi ng buhay hanggang sa kasalukuyan.
Isama ang mahahalagang detalye tulad ng edukasyon, karanasan, hamon, at mga tagumpay ng tao.
Gumamit ng malinaw at organisadong pagkakasulat upang lubos na maipakita ang buhay at ambag ng taong pinag-uusapan.

lessons.title: Synonyms and Antonyms
lessons.sub: Words with Similar and Opposite Meanings
learn: A synonym is a word that means almost the same thing as another word — like happy and glad, or big and large.
An antonym is a word that means the opposite of another word — like hot and cold, or fast and slow.
Learning synonyms helps writers avoid repeating the same word again and again, making their writing more interesting.
Learning antonyms helps readers understand contrast — like comparing two very different characters or ideas.
Context clues in a sentence can help you figure out whether a new word is a synonym or antonym of a word you already know.

lessons.title: Sequential Plot
lessons.sub: The Order of Events in a Story
learn: The plot of a story is the sequence of events — what happens first, next, and last.
Most stories follow this order: beginning (introduces characters and setting), middle (the problem or conflict happens), and end (the problem is solved).
Signal words like first, then, next, after that, and finally help readers follow the order of events.
Retelling a story in the correct sequence helps readers understand and remember what they read.
Mixing up the order of events can confuse the meaning of a story, so paying attention to sequence words is important.

lessons.title: Prefixes
lessons.sub: un-, in-, il-, ir-, im-, mis-, dis-
learn: A prefix is a word part added to the beginning of a word that changes its meaning.
un-, in-, il-, ir-, and im- usually mean "not" — like unhappy (not happy), incomplete (not complete), illegal (not legal), irregular (not regular), and impossible (not possible).
il- is used before words starting with l (illegal), ir- before words starting with r (irregular), and im- before words starting with m or p (impossible, immature).
mis- means "wrongly" — like misspell (spell wrongly) or misunderstand (understand wrongly).
dis- means "not" or "the opposite of" — like disagree (not agree) or dishonest (not honest).
Knowing prefixes helps you figure out the meaning of new words without needing a dictionary.

lessons.title: Suffixes
learn: A suffix is a word part added to the end of a word that can change its meaning or its part of speech.
-able and -ible mean "able to be" — like washable (able to be washed) or flexible (able to bend).
-ful means "full of" — like joyful (full of joy) — while -less means "without" — like fearless (without fear).
-ion turns a verb into a noun — like celebrate becomes celebration.
-er and -or often mean "a person who does something" — like teacher and actor.
-ly usually turns an adjective into an adverb — like quick becomes quickly — and -ness turns an adjective into a noun, like kind becomes kindness.

lessons.title: Compound Words
learn: A compound word is formed when two smaller words are joined together to make one new word with its own meaning.
Examples: sun + flower = sunflower, note + book = notebook, and rain + bow = rainbow.
Some compound words are written as one word (basketball), some with a hyphen (mother-in-law), and some as two separate words (ice cream).
You can often figure out the meaning of a compound word by thinking about the meanings of its two smaller words.

lessons.title: Outlining
lessons.sub: Topic, Main Idea, and Supporting Details
learn: An outline organizes information from a text in a clear, structured way before or after reading.
The topic is what the text is generally about, in just a word or short phrase.
The main idea is the most important point the writer wants to say about the topic.
Supporting details are the facts, examples, or explanations that back up the main idea.
Outlines usually use headings and sub-points (like Roman numerals or bullets) to show which details support which main idea.

lessons.title: Kinds of Verb
learn: A verb is a word that shows action or a state of being.
An action verb shows something a subject does, like run, jump, write, or think.
A linking verb connects the subject to more information about it, without showing action — like is, am, are, was, were, seem, and become.
Example: "She runs fast" uses an action verb, while "She is happy" uses a linking verb.
Identifying the verb in a sentence helps you understand what the sentence is really saying.

lessons.title: Simple Tenses of Verb
learn: Verb tense tells us when an action happens — in the past, present, or future.
Simple present tense shows things that happen regularly or facts — like "She walks to school."
Simple past tense shows actions that already happened — like "She walked to school."
Simple future tense shows actions that will happen — like "She will walk to school."
Most verbs form the simple past by adding -ed, but many common verbs are irregular, like go → went and eat → ate.

lessons.title: Subject-Verb Agreement
learn: Subject-verb agreement means the verb in a sentence must match the subject in number — singular subjects need singular verbs, and plural subjects need plural verbs.
A count noun can be counted and has a plural form — like one book, two books.

A mass noun (also called a non-count noun) cannot be counted individually — like rice, water, or information — and is usually treated as singular, so it takes a singular verb ("The rice is cooking.").

A collective noun names a group of people or things acting as one unit — like team, family, or class — and it usually takes a singular verb because the group acts together ("The team is practicing.").

lessons.title: Subject-Verb Agreement: More Noun Types
lessons.sub: Abstract and Concrete Nouns; Regular and Irregular Plurals
learn: A concrete noun names something you can see, hear, touch, taste, or smell — like dog, chair, or music.
An abstract noun names an idea, quality, or feeling that you cannot touch — like honesty, courage, or happiness. Abstract nouns are usually singular and take a singular verb.
A regular plural noun is formed by adding -s or -es to the singular form — like cat → cats, box → boxes.
An irregular plural noun changes its spelling in a different way — like child → children, mouse → mice, or foot → feet.
Whether a noun is singular or plural determines whether the verb should also be singular or plural, so the subject and verb agree.

lessons.title: Sequencing Events
learn: Sequencing means arranging events in the order in which they happened.
Clue words like first, second, next, meanwhile, afterward, and finally help readers identify the correct order of events.
Some texts are written out of time order, using flashbacks or jumping ahead — careful reading helps you figure out the real sequence.
Being able to sequence events correctly helps you understand cause and effect — what led to what.

lessons.title: Prefixes
lessons.sub: non-, anti-, de-, mal-, sub-, a-, under-
learn: non- means "not" — like nonfiction (not fiction) — while anti- means "against" — like antivirus (against a virus).
de- means "to remove" or "reverse" — like defrost (remove frost) — and mal- means "bad" or "wrongly" — like malnutrition (bad nutrition).
sub- means "under" or "below" — like submarine (under the sea/water) — while a- can mean "not" or "without" — like asymmetrical (not symmetrical).
under- means "below" or "not enough" — like underweight (not enough weight) or underground (below the ground).
Recognizing these prefixes helps you break down long or unfamiliar words into meaningful parts.

lessons.title: Suffixes
learn: -dom often means "a state or condition" — like freedom (state of being free) or kingdom (territory ruled by a king).
-ity and -ty turn adjectives into nouns describing a quality — like real → reality, and cruel → cruelty.
-ment turns a verb into a noun describing a result or process — like agree → agreement.
-ship describes a state, condition, or skill — like friendship or leadership.
-wise means "in the manner of" or "regarding" — like clockwise — while -al often turns a noun into an adjective, like nation → national.
-age can mean "a collection" or "a process" (like package or marriage), and -ious/-ous mean "full of" — like dangerous (full of danger).

lessons.title: Text Types
learn: Writers organize information using different text structures depending on their purpose.
Enumeration-description text lists facts or details about a topic, often one after another, without a strict order.
Chronological (time-order) text presents events in the order they happened, often with dates or time-signal words.
Procedural text gives step-by-step instructions on how to do something, like a recipe or a how-to guide.
Problem-solution text presents a problem and then explains one or more solutions to fix it.
Recognizing the text type helps readers know what to expect and how to find the information they need.

lessons.title: Subject-Verb Agreement: Pronouns (Part 1)
learn: A personal pronoun takes the place of a specific person or thing — like I, you, he, she, it, we, and they.
Singular personal pronouns (he, she, it) usually take a singular verb — "She sings." Plural personal pronouns (we, they) take a plural verb — "They sing."
An indefinite pronoun does not refer to a specific person or thing — like everyone, someone, nobody, few, and many.
Some indefinite pronouns are always singular (everyone, everybody, each, nobody) and need a singular verb, while others are always plural (several, few, many, both) and need a plural verb.

lessons.title: Subject-Verb Agreement: Pronouns (Part 2)
lessons.sub: Possessive Pronoun, Demonstrative Pronoun, and Possessive Noun
learn: A possessive pronoun shows ownership and replaces a noun — like mine, yours, his, hers, ours, and theirs.
A demonstrative pronoun points to specific things — this and that are singular, while these and those are plural — and the verb must agree with which one is used.
A possessive noun also shows ownership but is formed from a noun — usually by adding 's for singular nouns (the dog's bone) or just an apostrophe for plural nouns ending in s (the dogs' bones).

When a possessive noun or pronoun is the subject of a sentence, the verb must still agree with whether it refers to one thing or many — "The teacher's book is on the table" versus "The teachers' books are on the table."

lessons.title: Sound Devices
learn: Sound devices are techniques writers use to create rhythm and interesting sounds in their writing, especially in poems.
Onomatopoeia uses words that imitate the sound they describe — like buzz, splash, boom, and meow.
Alliteration repeats the same beginning consonant sound in nearby words — like "Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers."
Assonance repeats vowel sounds within nearby words — like the ee sound in "The sleek sea creatures leap."
Consonance repeats consonant sounds anywhere in nearby words, not just at the beginning — like the t sound in "pitter-patter."
Sound devices make writing more musical and help readers picture or feel what is happening.

lessons.title: Author's Point of View
lessons.sub: First, Second, and Third Person POV
learn: Point of view (POV) tells us who is narrating, or telling, the story.
First person POV uses pronouns like I, me, we, and us — the narrator is a character inside the story, sharing their own thoughts and experiences.
Second person POV uses the pronoun you, speaking directly to the reader as if they are part of the story — this is less common and often used in instructions or choose-your-own-adventure stories.
Third person POV uses pronouns like he, she, it, and they — the narrator is outside the story, describing the characters and events from a distance.
Identifying the point of view helps readers understand whose perspective and feelings are being shared in the story.

lessons.title: Adjectives
learn: An adjective is a word that describes or gives more information about a noun or pronoun.
A descriptive adjective tells more about the qualities of a noun — like its color, size, shape, or feeling — such as blue, tiny, round, or happy.
A numeral adjective tells the number or order of nouns — like three apples (cardinal number) or the third place (ordinal number).
Adjectives usually come right before the noun they describe, like "a bright red kite," or after a linking verb, like "The kite is bright."

lessons.title: Degrees of Regular and Irregular Adjectives
learn: Adjectives have degrees that show how something compares to other things: positive, comparative, and superlative.
The positive degree simply describes one noun without comparing it — like tall.
The comparative degree compares two nouns, usually adding -er or using "more" — like taller or more beautiful.
The superlative degree compares three or more nouns, usually adding -est or using "most" — like tallest or most beautiful.
Some adjectives are irregular and change completely in their comparative and superlative forms — like good → better → best, and bad → worse → worst.

lessons.title: Series of Adjectives
lessons.sub: Determiner, Quantity, Quality, Size, Shape, Color
learn: When two or more adjectives describe the same noun, they are usually arranged in a specific order, called a series of adjectives.
The typical order is: determiner (a, the, my), quantity (three, many), quality/opinion (beautiful, delicious), size (big, small), shape (round, square), and color (red, blue) — followed by the noun.
Example: "my two lovely small round red balloons" follows the correct order: determiner, quantity, quality, size, shape, color.
Commas are usually used to separate adjectives of the same type in a series, like "a happy, playful puppy."

lessons.title: Parts of a Sentence
learn: A sentence is a group of words that expresses a complete thought, and it has two main parts: the subject and the predicate.
The subject is who or what the sentence is about — usually a noun or pronoun.
The predicate tells what the subject does or is — it always contains the verb.
Example: in "The little puppy barked loudly," the subject is "the little puppy" and the predicate is "barked loudly."

lessons.title: Active and Passive Voice
learn: In the active voice, the subject performs the action of the verb — like "The boy kicked the ball."
In the passive voice, the subject receives the action, and the doer is often introduced with "by" or left out entirely — like "The ball was kicked by the boy."
Passive voice sentences often use a form of the verb "to be" (was, were, is, are) plus a past participle (like kicked, written, or made).
Active voice is usually clearer and more direct, while passive voice is useful when the doer of the action is unknown or unimportant.

lessons.title: Simple Sentence
learn: A simple sentence has just one independent clause — one subject and one predicate expressing a complete thought.
Example: "The children played in the park."
A simple sentence can still have more than one subject or verb, as long as it has only one complete thought — like "Anna and Ben played in the park."
Simple sentences are short and direct, making them useful for clear, easy-to-understand writing.

lessons.title: Compound Sentence
learn: A compound sentence joins two or more independent clauses (complete thoughts) that could each stand alone as their own sentence.
Independent clauses are usually joined using a comma and a coordinating conjunction — like and, but, or, so — or with a semicolon.
Example: "I wanted to play outside, but it started to rain."
Compound sentences show a relationship between two equally important ideas, like addition, contrast, or cause and effect.

lessons.title: Complex Sentence
learn: A complex sentence has one independent clause (a complete thought) and at least one dependent clause (an incomplete thought that needs the rest of the sentence).
Dependent clauses often begin with words like because, although, since, when, if, or after.
Example: "Because it started to rain, we stayed inside." — "Because it started to rain" is the dependent clause, and "we stayed inside" is the independent clause.
Complex sentences are useful for showing cause and effect, time relationships, or conditions between ideas.

lessons.title: Compound-Complex Sentence
learn: A compound-complex sentence combines at least two independent clauses and at least one dependent clause.

Example: "Because it started to rain, we stayed inside, and we watched a movie." This has one dependent clause ("Because it started to rain") and two independent clauses ("we stayed inside" and "we watched a movie").
This type of sentence lets writers express more complex relationships between several ideas at once.
Compound-complex sentences should still be punctuated carefully, using commas to separate the dependent clause and coordinating conjunctions to join the independent clauses.

f_q1c1l1.explain: Mali. Lumalago ang pagtitiwala sa sarili sa pamamagitan ng pagsubok sa mga bagong hamon at pagkatuto mula sa ating mga pagkakamali, hindi sa pagiging laging perpekto.
f_q1c1l1.q: Ang pagtitiwala sa sarili ay lumalago lamang kapag hindi tayo nagkakamali kailanman sa ating mga ginagawa.

f_q1c1l1.explain: Tama. Sa halip na sumuko sa pagkakamali, ang pagkatuto mula rito ay tumutulong upang lalong tumibay ang tiwala natin sa ating sarili.
f_q1c1l1.q: Ang pagkatuto mula sa sariling mga pagkakamali ay isang mahalagang paraan upang mapalago ang pagtitiwala sa sarili.

f_q1c1l1.explain: Mali. Ang kuwento ay nagtuturo sa mga bata na matutong magtiwala sa sarili at gumawa ng mga bagay nang mag-isa.
f_q1c1l1.q: Ang pangunahing aral ng kuwentong 'Kaya Ko!' ay turuan ang mga bata na umasa na lamang sa tulong ng ibang tao sa lahat ng pagkakataon.

f_q1c1l1.explain: Mali. Lumalago ang pagtitiwala sa sarili kapag hinaharap at sinusubukan natin ang mga bagong hamon, hindi kapag iniiwasan natin ang mga ito.
f_q1c1l1.q: Ang pag-iwas sa mga bagong hamon ang pinakamainam na paraan upang mapaunlad ang pagtitiwala sa sarili.

f_q1c1l1.explain: Tama. Kapag natutong gumawa ang bata nang mag-isa, nadarama niya na kaya niyang magtagumpay sa pamamagitan ng sariling sikap.
f_q1c1l1.q: Ang matutong gumawa ng mga bagay nang mag-isa ay nakatutulong sa isang bata upang magkaroon ng tiwala sa sariling kakayahan.

f_q1c1l1.explain: Ang positibong pag-iisip at pagsasalita nang mabuti sa sarili ay nagbibigay ng lakas ng loob upang harapin ang mga gawaing kinatatakutan.
f_q1c1l1.q: Ang pagpapasimula ng isang mahirap na gawain gamit ang positibong pananalita sa sarili tulad ng "Kaya ko ito" ay nakatutulong upang mabawasan ang takot at mas maging handa sa pagsubok.

f_q1c1l1.explain: Ang paghingi ng gabay kapag kinakailangan ay tanda ng pagnanais matuto at magwasto, at hindi nangangahulugang kawalan ng tiwala sa sarili.
f_q1c1l1.q: Ang paghingi ng gabay sa guro o magulang kapag nahihirapan sa aralin ay patunay na walang anumang tiwala sa sariling kakayahan ang isang mag-aaral.

f_q1c1l1.explain: Ang pagtitiwala sa sarili ay nagmumula sa sariling pag-unlad at hindi sa pagkumpara ng sarili sa kapwa.
f_q1c1l1.q: Ang tunay na pagtitiwala sa sarili ay nakatuon sa pagpapabuti ng sariling kakayahan araw-araw kaysa sa pakikipagpaligsahan upang patunayang mas magaling tayo sa iba.

f_q1c1l1.explain: Likas ang makaramdam ng kaba, ngunit ang taong may tiwala sa sarili ay patuloy na humaharap sa hamon kahit siya ay kinakabahan.
f_q1c1l1.q: Ang isang batang may matatag na tiwala sa sarili ay hindi kailanman nakararamdam ng kaba o takot kapag nagtatanghal sa harap ng maraming tao.

f_q1c1l1.explain: Ang ganap na pagtitiwala sa sarili ay nangangailangan ng pag-unawa sa ating mga kakayahan at sa mga bagay na dapat pa nating pagsumikapang mapagbuti.
f_q1c1l1.q: Ang pagtanggap sa sariling mga kahinaan ay kasinghalaga rin ng pagkilala sa sariling mga kalakasan upang magkaroon ng matapat na tiwala sa sarili.

f_q1c1l1.explain: Ang pagsuko pagkatapos ng unang pagkatalo ay nakababawas sa tiwala sa sarili; ang patuloy na pagsubok at pagkatuto ang tunay na nagpapatatag dito.
f_q1c1l1.q: Ang tuluyang pagtigil sa pagsubok pagkatapos ng unang pagkatalo ay nakatutulong upang mapangalagaan ang tiwala sa sarili.

f_q1c1l1.explain: Kapag nagtatagumpay tayo sa maliliit na bahagi ng gawain, unti-unting lumalakas ang ating paniniwala na kaya rin nating tapusin ang buong gawain.
f_q1c1l1.q: Ang paghahati ng isang malaking gawain sa maliliit na hakbang ay nakatutulong upang unti-unting mabuo ang tiwala sa sarili habang natatapos ang bawat bahagi nito.

f_q1c1l1.explain: Ang pagtitiwala sa sarili ay isang kasanayang natututuhan, naipapanatili, at napalalago sa pamamagitan ng pagsasanay at positibong karanasan.
f_q1c1l1.q: Ang pagtitiwala sa sarili ay isang katangiang taglay na ng tao mula pagkabata at hindi na mapauunlad pa sa pamamagitan ng pagsasanay at karanasan.

f_q1c1l1.explain: Ang lakas ng loob na magpahayag ng sariling opinyon nang may paggalang ay isang malinaw na palatandaan ng pagtitiwala sa sarili.
f_q1c1l1.q: Ang malayang pagbabahagi ng sariling ideya sa talakayan sa klase, kahit iba ito sa sagot ng karamihan, ay nagpapakita ng tiwala sa sariling kaisipan.

f_q1c1l1.explain: Ang tunay na tiwala sa sarili ay may kaakibat na kerendahan ng loob at pagiging bukas sa mga constructive feedback upang mas lalo pang mapabuti ang sarili.
f_q1c1l1.q: Ang pagkakaroon ng tiwala sa sarili ay nangangahulugan din ng pagiging mayabang at pag-aakalang hindi na kailangang makinig sa payo ng ibang tao.

f_q1c1l1.explain: Ang pagtitiwala sa sarili ay ang matatag na paniniwala sa sariling kakayahang matuto at humarap sa mga pagsubok sa buhay.
options: Ang paniniwala sa sariling kakayahan na matuto at makagawa ng mga bagay-bagay.
Ang pag-aakala na mas magaling tayo sa lahat ng ating mga kaklase.
Ang pagtanggi na humingi ng tulong sa kahit kanino kahit kailangan.
Ang pag-iwas sa mga gawaing may posibilidad na tayo ay magkamali.
f_q1c1l1.q: Ano ang totoong kahulugan ng pagkakaroon ng pagtitiwala sa sarili?

f_q1c1l1.explain: Kapag tayo ay nag-eensayo o nagsasanay nang mabuti, nagiging mas handa tayo kaya mas tumataas ang ating tiwala sa sarili.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ang karaniwang ayos ay Panaguri + Simuno. Ang di-karaniwang ayos ay Simuno + ay + Panaguri.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ayusin ang mga pangungusap sa Karaniwang Ayos o Di-karaniwang Ayos.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Tingnan kung nauuna ang panaguri o ang simuno.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ilagay ang bawat pangungusap sa tamang ayos.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ang salitang 'ay' ay madalas makita sa di-karaniwang ayos.

items.label: Si Ben ay tumutulong sa kapatid.

f_q1c1l2.q: Pag-uri-uriin ang mga pangungusap ayon sa ayos nito.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Karaniwang ayos: nauuna ang panaguri. Di-karaniwang ayos: nauuna ang simuno.
f_q1c1l2.q: Kilalanin ang uri ng ayos ng bawat pangungusap.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Uriin ayon sa pagkakasunod ng panaguri at simuno.
f_q1c1l2.q: I-drag ang mga pangungusap sa wastong kategorya.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Sa karaniwang ayos, nauuna ang panaguri bago ang simuno.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang karaniwang ayos ng pangungusap ay Panaguri + Simuno.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ang di-karaniwang ayos ay Simuno + ay + Panaguri.
f_q1c1l2.q: Sa di-karaniwang ayos, nauuna ang simuno at kadalasang may salitang 'ay'.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Nauuna ang panaguri kaya ito ay karaniwang ayos.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang pangungusap na 'Mabait si Ana.' ay nasa di-karaniwang ayos.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Nauuna ang simuno at may 'ay'.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang pangungusap na 'Si Ana ay mabait.' ay nasa di-karaniwang ayos.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Madaling makilala ang di-karaniwang ayos dahil sa paggamit ng 'ay'.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang salitang 'ay' ay karaniwang makikita sa di-karaniwang ayos ng pangungusap.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Nauuna ang panaguri na 'Masaya'.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang pangungusap na 'Masaya ang mga bata.' ay nasa karaniwang ayos.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ito ay di-karaniwang ayos dahil nauuna ang simuno.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang pangungusap na 'Ang mga bata ay masaya.' ay nasa karaniwang ayos.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ang simuno ang tinutukoy o pinag-uusapan.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang simuno ang paksa o pinag-uusapan sa pangungusap.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ang 'Mataas' ay panaguri at ang 'ang puno' ang simuno.
f_q1c1l2.q: Sa pangungusap na 'Mataas ang puno.', ang 'Mataas' ay simuno.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Nauuna ang panaguri na 'Nag-aaral'.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang pangungusap na 'Nag-aaral ang bata.' ay halimbawa ng karaniwang ayos.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Nauuna ang simuno at may 'ay'.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang pangungusap na 'Ang bata ay nag-aaral.' ay nasa di-karaniwang ayos.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ang panaguri ang nagbibigay-impormasyon tungkol sa simuno.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang panaguri ay nagsasabi ng tungkol sa simuno.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Magkaiba ang pagkakasunod ng simuno at panaguri.
f_q1c1l2.q: Pareho lamang ang karaniwang ayos at di-karaniwang ayos ng pangungusap.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Nauuna ang panaguri na 'Maganda'.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang 'Maganda ang bulaklak.' ay nasa karaniwang ayos.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Nauuna ang simuno at kasunod ang panaguri.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang 'Ang bulaklak ay maganda.' ay nasa di-karaniwang ayos.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Sa karaniwang ayos, panaguri ang nauuna.
f_q1c1l2.q: Sa karaniwang ayos, laging nauuna ang simuno.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Panaguri muna bago simuno.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang pangungusap na 'Tumatakbo ang aso.' ay nasa karaniwang ayos.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Simuno muna bago panaguri.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang pangungusap na 'Ang aso ay tumatakbo.' ay nasa di-karaniwang ayos.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ang 'ang puno' ang simuno ng pangungusap.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang 'ang puno' sa pangungusap na 'Mataas ang puno.' ay panaguri.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Nagbabago lamang ang ayos ng simuno at panaguri ngunit hindi ang pangunahing kahulugan.
f_q1c1l2.q: Maaaring magkapareho ang kahulugan ng karaniwang ayos at di-karaniwang ayos ngunit magkaiba ang pagkakasunod ng mga bahagi nito.

f_q1c1l2.explain: May buong diwa at kumpletong kaisipan.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang "Masayang naglalaro ang mga bata sa parke." ay isang pangungusap.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Hindi ito nagpapahayag ng buong kaisipan.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang "Sa ilalim ng malaking puno" ay isang pangungusap.

f_q1c1l2.explain: May simuno at panaguri at buo ang diwa.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang "Nagbabasa si Ana ng aklat." ay isang pangungusap.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Parirala lamang ito at walang buong diwa.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang "Mga pulang bulaklak sa hardin" ay isang pangungusap.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Kumpleto ang ipinahahayag na kaisipan.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang "Maagang pumasok sa paaralan si Ben." ay isang pangungusap.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Hindi nito sinasabi ang buong mensahe.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang "Sa ibabaw ng mesa" ay isang pangungusap.

f_q1c1l2.explain: May buong diwa at malinaw na paksa.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang "Masarap ang nilutong adobo ni Nanay." ay isang pangungusap.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Hindi ito nagsasaad ng ganap na kaisipan.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang "Mga laruan ng aking kapatid" ay isang pangungusap.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Naghahayag ito ng isang buong ideya.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang "Tumutulong si Carlo sa paglilinis ng silid." ay isang pangungusap.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Hindi kumpleto ang ipinahahayag na kaisipan.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang "Habang umuulan nang malakas" ay isang pangungusap.

f_q1c1l2.explain: May buong mensahe at kumpletong diwa.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang "Nagtanim kami ng gulay kahapon." ay isang pangungusap.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Parirala lamang ito.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang "Malapit sa ilog" ay isang pangungusap.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Kumpleto ang kaisipang ipinahahayag.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang "Masaya ang pamilya sa kanilang bakasyon." ay isang pangungusap.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Wala itong buong diwa.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang "Sa loob ng silid-aralan" ay isang pangungusap.

f_q1c1l2.explain: May kumpletong mensahe ito.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang "Nagwagi ang aming koponan sa paligsahan." ay isang pangungusap.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Hindi buo ang kaisipan at tila may kulang pa.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang "Pagkatapos ng mahabang paglalakbay patungong probinsiya" ay isang pangungusap.

f_q1c1l2.explain: May buong diwa at malinaw na mensahe.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang "Kahit pagod mula sa ensayo, nagawa pa rin ni Lea ang kanyang takdang-aralin." ay isang pangungusap.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Walang panaguring nagbibigay ng buong kaisipan.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang "Ang mga batang masisipag sa pag-aaral at palaging handa sa klase" ay isang pangungusap.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ganap ang kaisipan at may malinaw na mensahe.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang "Nakapag-ulat nang mahusay ang pangkat kahit kulang sila sa oras ng paghahanda." ay isang pangungusap.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Hindi ito nagpapahayag ng kumpletong ideya.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ang "Sa gitna ng malakas na hangin at walang tigil na ulan" ay isang pangungusap.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ang pangungusap ay may buong diwa at kumpletong kaisipan.

f_q1c1l2.q: Pagbukud-bukurin ang mga halimbawa ayon sa uri.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ang simuno ay pinag-uusapan sa pangungusap, habang ang panag-uri ay nagsasabi ng ginagawa o sinasabi tungkol sa simuno.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ayusin ang mga parirala sa tamang kategorya: Simuno o Panag-uri.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Hanapin kung sino o ano ang pinag-uusapan (simuno) at kung ano ang sinasabi tungkol dito (panag-uri).
f_q1c1l2.q: Ilagay sa tamang pangkat ang bawat bahagi ng pangungusap.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ang simuno ay paksa ng pangungusap, at ang panag-uri ay nagbibigay ng impormasyon tungkol dito.
f_q1c1l2.q: Pag-uri-uriin ang mga sumusunod bilang Simuno o Panag-uri.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Tukuyin kung ang parirala ay tumutukoy sa paksa o sa ginagawa ng paksa.
f_q1c1l2.q: Ayusin ang bawat salita o parirala sa tamang kategorya.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ang panag-uri ay nagsasabi ng kilos o kalagayan ng simuno.
f_q1c1l2.q: Pagbukud-bukurin ang mga halimbawa ayon sa Simuno o Panag-uri.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ang simuno ang pinag-uusapan sa pangungusap.
f_q1c1l2.q: Sa pangungusap na "Si Ana ay nagbabasa ng aklat.", ang "Si Ana" ay simuno.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ang panag-uri ang nagsasabi ng ginagawa o kalagayan ng simuno.
f_q1c1l2.q: Sa pangungusap na "Masayang naglalaro ang mga bata.", ang "Masayang naglalaro" ay panag-uri.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ito ay panag-uri dahil ito ang ginagawa ng aso.
f_q1c1l2.q: Sa pangungusap na "Ang aso ay tumatahol nang malakas.", ang "tumatahol nang malakas" ay simuno.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Si Ben ang pinag-uusapan sa pangungusap.
f_q1c1l2.q: Sa pangungusap na "Si Ben ay maagang pumasok sa paaralan.", ang "Si Ben" ay simuno.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ito ay simuno.
f_q1c1l2.q: Sa pangungusap na "Ang mga ibon ay lumilipad sa himpapawid.", ang "Ang mga ibon" ay panag-uri.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ito ang sinasabi tungkol sa simuno.
f_q1c1l2.q: Sa pangungusap na "Ang guro ay nagtuturo ng matematika.", ang "nagtuturo ng matematika" ay panag-uri.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Si Carla ang pinag-uusapan sa pangungusap.
f_q1c1l2.q: Sa pangungusap na "Masipag mag-aral si Carla.", ang "si Carla" ay simuno.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ito ang paksa ng pangungusap.
f_q1c1l2.q: Sa pangungusap na "Ang hardinero ay nagdidilig ng mga halaman.", ang "Ang hardinero" ay simuno.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ito ay panag-uri.
f_q1c1l2.q: Sa pangungusap na "Naglilinis ng silid ang mga mag-aaral.", ang "Naglilinis ng silid" ay simuno.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ito ang nagsasabi ng kilos ng simuno.
f_q1c1l2.q: Sa pangungusap na "Ang tren ay dumating nang maaga.", ang "dumating nang maaga" ay panag-uri.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ito ang kilos ng simuno.
f_q1c1l2.q: Sa pangungusap na "Si Liza ay umaawit sa entablado.", ang "umaawit sa entablado" ay panag-uri.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Sila ang pinag-uusapan sa pangungusap.
f_q1c1l2.q: Sa pangungusap na "Ang mga turista ay bumisita sa museo.", ang "Ang mga turista" ay simuno.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ito ay simuno.
f_q1c1l2.q: Sa pangungusap na "Mabilis tumakbo ang kabayo.", ang "ang kabayo" ay panag-uri.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ito ang ginawa ng doktor.
f_q1c1l2.q: Sa pangungusap na "Ang doktor ay tumulong sa pasyente.", ang "tumulong sa pasyente" ay panag-uri.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ito ang nagsasabi ng katangian ng simuno.
f_q1c1l2.q: Sa pangungusap na "Ang ilog ay malinis at malinaw.", ang "malinis at malinaw" ay panag-uri.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Kahit nasa hulihan, ito pa rin ang simuno.
f_q1c1l2.q: Sa pangungusap na "Sa paligsahan ay nagwagi ang aming pangkat.", ang "ang aming pangkat" ay simuno.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Bahagi ito ng panag-uri, hindi simuno.
f_q1c1l2.q: Sa pangungusap na "Masayang-masaya ang mga bata dahil walang pasok.", ang "dahil walang pasok" ay simuno.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Siya ang pinag-uusapan sa pangungusap.
f_q1c1l2.q: Sa pangungusap na "Nakapag-ulat nang mahusay ang lider ng pangkat.", ang "ang lider ng pangkat" ay simuno.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ito ang buong simuno ng pangungusap.
f_q1c1l2.q: Sa pangungusap na "Ang batang masipag at matiyaga ay nagtagumpay sa proyekto.", ang "Ang batang masipag at matiyaga" ay simuno.

f_q1c1l2.explain: Ito ay pariralang nagbibigay-karagdagang impormasyon; ang simuno ay "ang mga mag-aaral".
f_q1c1l2.q: Sa pangungusap na "Matapos ang mahabang ensayo, mahusay na nagtanghal ang mga mag-aaral.", ang "Matapos ang mahabang ensayo" ay simuno.

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 4,250 + 1,375 - 825 = 4,800. The 96 pages are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: Mia had 4,250 stickers. She bought 1,375 more and gave 825 stickers to her friend. Her notebook has 96 pages. How many stickers does Mia have now?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 8,500 + 1,250 - 675 = 9,075. The 12 shelves are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: A school library had 8,500 books. It received 1,250 new books and removed 675 old books. The library has 12 shelves. How many books are there now?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 3,600 + 1,450 - 875 = 4,175. The 4 wheels are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: Carlo saved ₱3,600. He received ₱1,450 as a gift and spent ₱875 on a toy. His toy had 4 wheels. How much money does Carlo have left?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 6,750 - 2,350 + 1,125 = 5,525. The 85 banana trees are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: A farmer harvested 6,750 mangoes. He sold 2,350 mangoes and harvested another 1,125 the next day. He also has 85 banana trees. How many mangoes does he have now?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 9,200 + 2,450 - 3,175 = 8,475. The 15 boxes are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: A store had 9,200 pencils. It received 2,450 more pencils and sold 3,175 pencils. There were 15 boxes on the shelf. How many pencils are left?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 5,800 + 2,275 - 1,650 = 6,425. The 20 students are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: A school collected 5,800 plastic bottles. Students collected 2,275 more bottles but sent 1,650 bottles for recycling. There were 20 students in one group. How many bottles does the school have now?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 7,500 + 1,875 - 2,625 = 6,750. The 50 cakes are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: A bakery made 7,500 bread rolls. It baked 1,875 more and sold 2,625 rolls. The bakery also made 50 cakes. How many bread rolls are left?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 4,675 + 1,325 - 950 = 5,050. The 32 animals are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: A zoo had 4,675 visitors on Saturday. On Sunday, 1,325 more visitors came, but 950 visitors left early. The zoo has 32 different animals. How many visitors remained?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 10,000 + 3,250 - 4,375 = 8,875. The 25 workers are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: A warehouse had 10,000 boxes. It received 3,250 new boxes and delivered 4,375 boxes. There were 25 workers in the warehouse. How many boxes are left?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 12,500 + 2,750 - 4,325 = 10,925. The 100 bags of rice are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: A charity group collected 12,500 canned goods. People donated 2,750 more cans, and the group gave 4,325 cans to families. They also collected 100 bags of rice. How many canned goods are left?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 15,750 + 8,425 - 6,875 = 17,300. The 24 classrooms are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: A school had 15,750 sheets of paper. It bought 8,425 more sheets and used 6,875 sheets for projects. The school has 24 classrooms. How many sheets of paper are left?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 24,600 + 7,850 - 9,475 = 22,975. The 50 books per shelf is a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: A bookstore had 24,600 books. It received 7,850 new books and sold 9,475 books. Each shelf can hold 50 books. How many books are left?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 18,750 + 6,325 - 9,875 = 15,200. The 125 sacks are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: A farmer harvested 18,750 kilograms of rice. He harvested another 6,325 kilograms and sold 9,875 kilograms. He used 125 sacks to store the rice. How many kilograms of rice remain?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 32,500 + 8,750 - 17,625 = 23,625. The 45 workers are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: A factory made 32,500 toys in January. It made 8,750 more toys in February and shipped 17,625 toys to stores. The factory has 45 workers. How many toys remain?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 27,850 + 6,475 - 12,650 = 21,675. The 300 boxes are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: A charity collected 27,850 canned goods. Another group donated 6,475 cans, and 12,650 cans were given to families. They also received 300 boxes. How many canned goods are left?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 35,000 - 28,475 - 3,250 = 3,275. The 15 security guards are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: A stadium had 35,000 seats. During a game, 28,475 people entered, and 3,250 more people arrived later. There were 15 security guards at each entrance. How many seats were still empty?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 42,750 + 13,625 - 21,875 = 34,500. The 36 loading areas are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: A warehouse stored 42,750 boxes. It received 13,625 more boxes, then delivered 21,875 boxes. The warehouse has 36 loading areas. How many boxes are left?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 48,500 + 12,750 - 26,875 = 34,375. The 125 students are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: A school raised ₱48,500 for a project. Parents donated another ₱12,750, and the school spent ₱26,875 on materials. There were 125 students who joined the project. How much money is left?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 36,450 + 9,875 - 14,625 = 31,700. The 18 sections are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: A library had 36,450 books. It received 9,875 donated books, then removed 14,625 damaged books. The library has 18 sections. How many books are there now?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 50,000 + 15,750 - 28,625 = 37,125. The 250 packs per truck are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: A food bank had 50,000 food packs. It received 15,750 more packs and distributed 28,625 packs to different communities. Each truck could carry 250 packs. How many food packs remain?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 62,500 + 18,750 - 24,325 = 56,925. The 15 crowns are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: King Julien had 62,500 coconuts stored for his kingdom. He gathered 18,750 more coconuts and used 24,325 coconuts for a royal feast. He also owns 15 crowns. How many coconuts does King Julien have now?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 45,800 + 22,150 - 17,925 = 50,025. The 4 penguins are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: Private had 45,800 bird seeds stored in the base. He collected 22,150 more seeds and gave away 17,925 seeds to a nearby flock. There are 4 penguins on the team. How many bird seeds does Private have now?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 78,600 + 25,475 - 39,850 = 64,225. The 12 palm trees are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: Maurice managed King Julien's treasury of 78,600 gold coins. He earned 25,475 more coins from trade and spent 39,850 coins on royal decorations. The kingdom has 12 palm trees. How many gold coins are left?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 91,250 + 17,825 - 28,650 = 80,425. The 5 tanks are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: Skipper counted 91,250 fish in the aquarium tank. The team caught 17,825 more fish, but 28,650 fish swam away during the storm. There are 5 tanks in the aquarium. How many fish remain?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 56,750 + 19,325 - 32,875 = 43,200. The 3 decks are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: Kowalski calculated that the ship had 56,750 liters of fuel. He added 19,325 more liters after refueling and used 32,875 liters during the voyage. The ship has 3 decks. How many liters of fuel are left?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 34,600 + 21,750 - 12,325 = 44,025. The 2 giant rocks are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: Mort collected 34,600 leaves for King Julien's throne. He gathered another 21,750 leaves but lost 12,325 leaves in the wind. Mort walked past 2 giant rocks. How many leaves does Mort have now?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 67,850 + 29,475 - 18,600 = 78,725. The 20 animal shows are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: Alex the lion had 67,850 tickets printed for the zoo show. He sold 29,475 more tickets but refunded 18,600 tickets to unhappy customers. The zoo has 20 animal shows. How many tickets remain?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 82,400 + 26,750 - 19,325 = 89,825. The 4 legs are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: Marty the zebra counted 82,400 hoofprints in the sand. He made 26,750 more hoofprints during a race, but the tide washed away 19,325 hoofprints. Marty has 4 legs. How many hoofprints remain?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 73,500 + 24,875 - 31,650 = 66,725. The 8 vines are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: Melman the giraffe measured 73,500 centimeters of vines in the jungle. He found 24,875 more centimeters of vines but used 31,650 centimeters to build a treehouse. There are 8 vines in the treehouse frame. How many centimeters of vines are left?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 88,250 + 15,475 - 27,850 = 75,875. The 10 lily pads are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: Gloria the hippo had 88,250 kilograms of mud in her pool. Rainfall added 15,475 more kilograms, but the sun dried up 27,850 kilograms. The pool holds 10 lily pads. How many kilograms of mud are left?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 96,700 + 23,825 - 41,375 = 79,150. The 4 penguins are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: Rico hoarded 96,700 spare parts in his secret stash. He swallowed 23,825 more parts but used 41,375 parts to fix the boat. There are 4 penguins on the team. How many spare parts are left?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 105,600 + 32,475 - 48,650 = 89,425. The 6 judges are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: King Julien counted 105,600 votes from the lemurs for the annual dance contest. Another 32,475 votes came in, but 48,650 votes were disqualified. The contest had 6 judges. How many votes remain valid?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 118,750 + 45,325 - 62,875 = 101,200. The 9 watchtowers are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: Private guarded 118,750 crates of fish supplies at the base. The team delivered 45,325 more crates but used 62,875 crates for the winter stock. The base has 9 watchtowers. How many crates are left?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 124,300 + 38,750 - 55,625 = 107,425. The 14 shelves are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: Maurice organized 124,300 leaf-scrolls for the royal library. He added 38,750 more leaf-scrolls but gave away 55,625 leaf-scrolls to other lemurs. The library has 14 shelves. How many leaf-scrolls remain?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 142,600 + 47,875 - 63,250 = 127,225. The 5 lifeboats are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: Skipper tracked 142,600 nautical miles traveled by the team. They sailed 47,875 more miles but had to backtrack 63,250 miles because of a storm. The ship has 5 lifeboats. How many net miles have they truly traveled?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 156,750 + 42,325 - 68,875 = 130,200. The 3 assistants are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: Kowalski invented gadgets worth 156,750 zoo bucks. He sold gadgets worth 42,325 more zoo bucks but had to refund 68,875 zoo bucks for a malfunction. Kowalski has 3 assistants. How many zoo bucks does he have now?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 89,400 + 34,725 - 27,850 = 96,275. The 12 favorite shells are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: Mort collected 89,400 seashells on the beach. He found 34,725 more shells but lost 27,850 shells in the tide. Mort has 12 favorite shells. How many shells does he have now?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 165,800 + 52,475 - 74,650 = 143,625. The 40 animal exhibits are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: Alex performed for 165,800 zoo visitors over the year. Attendance increased by 52,475 more visitors, but 74,650 visitors left early during a rainstorm. The zoo has 40 animal exhibits. How many visitors stayed until the end?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 178,250 + 61,325 - 89,475 = 150,100. The 7 food stations are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: Gloria hosted 178,250 guests at the annual jungle party. Later, 61,325 more guests arrived, and 89,475 guests left before the fireworks. There were 7 food stations. How many guests remained for the fireworks?

mt_q1c2l1.explain: 192,600 + 68,750 - 115,325 = 146,025. The 25 castle rooms are a distractor number.
mt_q1c2l1.q: King Julien's treasury reached 192,600 gold coins after tax season. Maurice added 68,750 more coins from trade deals, but the kingdom spent 115,325 coins on a new castle. There are 25 castle rooms. How many gold coins remain?
