q1c1l2.q: Which of the following science tools is used for measuring bigger volumes of liquids?

q1c1l2.explain: Under the Standard Units of Measurement notes, 1 mL is equal to 1 cc (cubic centimeter).
q1c1l2.q: According to the standard metric units in the lesson, 1 milliliter (mL) is equal to:

q1c1l2.explain: Communicating is defined as sharing your observations, knowledge, and experiences from a science activity.
q1c1l2.q: Sharing your observations, knowledge, and experiences from a science activity with others is known as which process skill?

q1c1l2.explain: The standard metric units for measuring mass are grams (g) or kilograms (kg).
q1c1l2.q: Which metric units should you use when measuring the mass of a material?

q1c1l2.explain: Comparing is defined as identifying similarities or differences between things.
options: To identify similarities or differences between things
To measure the exact length of an object
To share information with other scientists
q1c1l2.q: What is the main purpose of the 'Comparing' process skill?

q1c1l2.explain: Stating that a damaged bill can be replaced by banks is an inference based on gathered information, not a direct observation made by the five senses.
options: The Php 1,000 bill has the image of an eagle.
If the Php 1,000 bill is damaged, then it can be replaced by banks.
The Php 1,000 bill is rectangular in shape.
q1c1l2.q: Based on the lesson quiz examples, which of the following statements about a Php 1,000 bill is an INFERENCE?

q1c1l2.explain: Classifying is sorting objects or events into groups by similar characteristics or categories.
q1c1l2.q: If you are sorting your clothes according to how they are used, which science process skill are you practicing?

q1c2l1.explain: Melting, evaporation, and sublimation all absorb heat from their surroundings. Freezing, condensation, and deposition all release heat.
q1c2l1.q: Sort each phase change into whether it absorbs heat or releases heat.

q1c2l1.explain: Phase changes can be useful, like preserving food or shaping metals. But too much evaporation, unwanted condensation, or melting glaciers cause problems like droughts, mold, and flooding.

items.label: Freezing meat and food to preserve them
Melting metals to shape them into cans and utensils
Too much evaporation drying out farmlands and causing drought
Indoor condensation damping walls and growing mold
Melting glaciers raising sea levels and flooding low areas

q1c2l1.q: Classify these effects of phase changes as either a useful effect or an unwanted effect.

q1c2l1.explain: Sublimation and deposition change directly between solid and gas without turning into a liquid first. Melting, freezing, evaporation, and condensation all involve a liquid phase.
q1c2l1.q: Group these phase changes based on whether they skip the liquid phase completely or involve a liquid.

q1c2l1.explain: Sublimation occurs when a solid changes directly to a gas (like dry ice). Deposition occurs when a gas changes directly into a solid (like snow frost on plants).

items.label: Dry ice turning directly to smoke
A solid changes directly to gas
Water vapor turning into frost on plants on cold nights
A gas changes directly to solid

q1c2l1.q: Sort the examples and descriptions into the correct direct phase change process.

q1c2l1.explain: Melting and condensation turn matter into a liquid state. Evaporation and sublimation turn matter into a gas state.
q1c2l1.q: Sort each phase change by the end result of matter produced.

q1c2l1.explain: According to the lesson, temperature goes UP when heat is absorbed.
q1c2l1.q: What happens to the temperature of matter when heat is absorbed?

q1c2l1.explain: Simmering happens when a liquid starts changing into gas right before it fully boils.
q1c2l1.q: What do we call the process where a liquid starts changing into gas right before it fully boils?

q1c2l1.explain: Vaporization happens at the boiling point of water, which is 100°C or above.
q1c2l1.q: At what temperature does vaporization happen, turning all liquid water into gas?

q1c2l1.explain: A physical change is a change in appearance (shape or form) without changing its composition.
options: A change in appearance without changing composition
A change that creates a brand new substance
A change that only happens when matter freezes
A change where the temperature never changes
q1c2l1.q: What is the definition of a physical change?

q1c2l1.explain: Melting is useful because it allows metals to be shaped into cans, utensils, and toys.
options: It shapes metals into cans, utensils, and toys
It stops mold from growing on walls
q1c2l1.q: How is melting useful in making everyday items?

q1c2l1.explain: Condensation stuck indoors without ventilation damps walls, corrodes paint, and grows mold.
options: It damps walls, corrodes paint, and grows mold
q1c2l1.q: What unwanted effect can happen if indoor condensation has no ventilation?

q1c2l1.explain: The lesson specifically mentions Navotas and Malabon as low-lying areas that can flood when melting glaciers raise sea levels.
q1c2l1.q: Which low-lying areas are mentioned as being at risk of flooding if glaciers melt?

q1c2l1.explain: Dew on leaves is an example of condensation, where gas turns into liquid water droplets.
q1c2l1.q: What is an example of condensation given in the lesson?

q1c2l1.explain: Freezing happens when a liquid releases heat and turns into a solid.
q1c2l1.q: What happens to heat during the freezing process?

q1c2l1.explain: Condensation turns water vapor into rain, snow, sleet, or hail, which are key steps in the water cycle.
q1c2l1.q: Which process turns water vapor into rain, snow, sleet, or hail in the water cycle?

q1c2l1.explain: When heat is released from matter, its temperature goes down.
q1c2l1.q: What happens to the temperature of matter when heat is released?

q1c2l1.explain: Freezing is a useful phase change because it helps preserve meat and food.
options: It cools the environment by removing heat
It creates rain and snow in the water cycle
q1c2l1.q: According to the lesson, how is freezing useful in our daily lives?

q1c2l1.explain: Sublimation occurs when a solid changes directly into a gas, skipping the liquid phase entirely.
q1c2l1.q: Which phase change happens when dry ice turns straight into smoke without turning into a liquid first?

q1c2l1.explain: Deposition is the process where a gas changes directly into a solid, skipping the liquid phase.
q1c2l1.q: On very cold nights, water vapor in the air can turn directly into snow frost on plants. What is this direct phase change called?

q1c2l1.explain: Too much evaporation removes a lot of water from the soil, drying out farmlands and potentially causing a drought.
options: It damps indoor walls and grows mold
It dries out farmlands and can cause drought
It corrodes paint on metal cans
It releases ancient viruses into the air
q1c2l1.q: What unwanted effect can happen if there is too much evaporation?

q1c2l1.explain: The lesson notes that melting glaciers may release ancient viruses and bacteria.
options: It can cause severe indoor mold
It may release ancient viruses and bacteria
It can stop the water cycle completely
It turns all ocean water into water vapor
q1c2l1.q: Besides raising sea levels and flooding low-lying areas, what other unwanted effect can melting glaciers cause?

q1c2l1.explain: Evaporation cools the environment because heat from the surroundings is absorbed during the process.
options: It shapes metals into cans and toys
It cools the environment by removing heat
It freezes water vapor into snow
q1c2l1.q: How does evaporation help the environment in a useful way?

q1c2l1.explain: Ice starts to melt from a solid into a liquid when the temperature goes above 0°C.
q1c2l1.q: At what temperature does ice start to melt into liquid water?

q1c2l1.explain: A phase change is a physical change where matter is exposed to heat or cold conditions.
options: A change in the chemical makeup of matter
A physical change where matter is exposed to heat or cold conditions
The process of heat rising above 100°C only
A permanent change where matter cannot turn back
q1c2l1.q: How do the lesson notes define a phase change?

q1c2l1.explain: According to the review notes, dry ice is made when carbon dioxide undergoes a phase change.
q1c2l1.q: Dry ice is made when which gas undergoes a phase change?

q1c2l1.explain: Melting and evaporation happen when matter absorbs heat. Freezing and condensation happen when heat is released.
q1c2l1.q: Sort each phase change based on whether matter absorbs heat or releases heat during the process.

q1c2l1.explain: Freezing food and melting metals to shape items are useful. Too much evaporation drying farmlands and indoor condensation dampening walls are unwanted effects.

items.label: Shaping metals into cans and toys
Drying out farmlands and causing drought
Damping indoor walls and growing mold

q1c2l1.q: Sort these phase change outcomes into useful effects or unwanted effects.

q1c2l1.explain: Freezing involves solid and liquid. Evaporation involves liquid and gas. Sublimation and deposition change directly between solid and gas without becoming a liquid.
q1c2l1.q: Sort each phase change according to the states of matter it transitions between.

q1c2l1.explain: Simmering is when liquid starts turning into gas right before boiling. Vaporization is when ALL liquid turns into gas at 100°C or above.

items.label: A liquid starts changing into gas right before fully boiling
ALL the liquid water turns to gas
Happens at the boiling point of 100°C or above

q1c2l1.q: Sort these descriptions into the correct process: Simmering or Vaporization.

q1c2l1.explain: Dew and droplets on a cold glass show condensation (gas to liquid). Dry ice smoking is sublimation (solid to gas). Snow frost on plants is deposition (gas to solid).

items.label: Water droplets on a cold glass
Dry ice turning straight into smoke
Snow frost forming on plants on cold nights

q1c2l1.q: Sort these real-world examples into their correct phase change process.

q1c2l1.explain: According to the lesson, temperature goes UP when heat is absorbed by matter.
q1c2l1.q: What happens to the temperature of matter when heat is absorbed?

q1c2l1.explain: A physical change is a change in appearance (shape/form) without changing composition.
options: A change in appearance (shape or form) without changing composition
A change that creates a brand new chemical substance
A change that permanently destroys matter
A change that only occurs when heat is released
q1c2l1.q: How do the lesson notes define a physical change?

q1c2l1.explain: Simmering is when a liquid starts changing into gas, right before it fully boils.
q1c2l1.q: What is happening when a liquid starts changing into gas, right before it fully boils?

q1c2l1.explain: Vaporization occurs at the boiling point of water, which is 100°C or above.
q1c2l1.q: At what temperature does vaporization happen for liquid water?

q1c2l1.explain: Melting is useful because it helps shape metals into cans, utensils, and toys.
options: It shapes metals into cans, utensils, and toys
It preserves meat and other food
It cools the environment by removing heat
It creates rain and snow in the water cycle
q1c2l1.q: According to the lesson, how is the process of melting useful?

q1c2l1.explain: Melting, evaporation, and sublimation all require matter to absorb heat.
q1c2l1.q: Which of these groups contains phase changes that all ABSORB heat?

q1c2l1.explain: Deposition is the phase change where a gas turns directly into a solid without becoming a liquid first.
q1c2l1.q: Which process describes a gas changing directly into a solid, skipping the liquid phase?

q1c2l1.explain: During vaporization, ALL the liquid water turns to gas at the boiling point.
options: ALL the liquid water turns to gas
Liquid water starts changing to gas right before boiling
Gas turns directly into a solid
Solid ice turns directly into gas
q1c2l1.q: What happens during full vaporization?

q1c2l1.explain: Melting (solid to liquid) and freezing (liquid to solid) are the phase changes between solid and liquid.
q1c2l1.q: Which two phase changes occur specifically between the solid and liquid states of matter?

q1c2l1.explain: During condensation, heat is released (removed) from a gas so it turns into liquid.
options: Heat is released from the gas
Heat is absorbed by the gas
Heat stays trapped inside the solid
Heat turns the gas directly into ice
q1c2l1.q: What happens to heat during condensation?

q1c2l1.explain: Without proper ventilation, indoor condensation builds up moisture that damps walls, corrodes paint, and allows mold to grow.
q1c2l1.q: Condensation trapped indoors without proper ventilation can damp walls, corrode paint, and grow mold.

q1c2l1.explain: Freezing happens when a liquid releases heat to become a solid. Melting, evaporation, and sublimation are the phase changes that absorb heat.
q1c2l1.q: Freezing is a phase change where matter absorbs heat from its surroundings.

q1c2l1.explain: Temperature goes down when heat is released by matter, and goes up when heat is absorbed.
q1c2l1.q: When heat is released from matter, its temperature goes up.

q1c2l1.explain: Deposition occurs when a gas changes directly into a solid without becoming a liquid first, like water vapor turning into snow frost.
q1c2l1.q: Water vapor changing directly into snow frost on very cold nights is an example of deposition.

q1c2l1.explain: Sublimation happens when a solid turns directly into a gas without melting into a liquid first, which is what dry ice does.
q1c2l1.q: Dry ice turning directly into smoke or gas is a real-life example of sublimation.

q1c2l1.explain: Sublimation skips the liquid phase completely, changing a solid directly into a gas.
q1c2l1.q: Sublimation is a phase change where a solid must first melt into a liquid before it can turn into a gas.

q1c2l1.explain: Melting glaciers raise sea levels, causing unwanted flooding in low-lying areas such as Navotas and Malabon.
q1c2l1.q: Melting glaciers are beneficial because they lower sea levels and prevent flooding in coastal areas.

q1c2l1.explain: Condensation changes water vapor in the atmosphere into liquid or solid precipitation like rain, snow, sleet, or hail.
q1c2l1.q: Condensation turns water vapor into rain, snow, sleet, or hail, which are key steps in the water cycle.

q1c2l1.explain: Excessive evaporation is an unwanted effect because it dries out farmlands and can lead to drought.
q1c2l1.q: Too much evaporation is helpful to farmlands because it keeps the soil wet.

q1c2l1.explain: Freezing preserves food and meat by keeping them cold, preventing them from spoiling quickly.
q1c2l1.q: Freezing is a useful phase change because it helps preserve meat and other food.

q1c2l2.explain: Melting ice and boiling water change only the form of matter (physical change), while iron rusting and burning paper form new materials (chemical change).
q1c2l2.q: Sort each example into whether it is a Physical Change or a Chemical Change.

q1c2l2.explain: Digestion and photosynthesis help living things survive, while acid rain and soil contamination cause harm to nature and structures.

items.label: Digestion breaking food down for the body
Acid rain destroying metals and buildings
Harmful chemicals leaching into soil from dump sites

q1c2l2.q: Sort these effects of chemical changes into Useful Effects or Undesirable Effects.

q1c2l2.explain: Cutting an apple, inflating a tire, and absorbing water change only form, shape, or state. Cooking a pancake, wood rotting, and milk souring create new materials.
q1c2l2.q: Sort these quick quiz items from the lesson into Physical Change or Chemical Change.

q1c2l2.explain: Soot, dust, and ash are solid particles floating in the air (particulates), while carbon monoxide and oxides of sulfur/nitrogen are poisonous gases.
q1c2l2.q: Sort these air pollutants into Particulates or Toxic Gases based on the lesson notes.

q1c2l2.explain: Acid rain and breathing particulates are caused by air pollution, while sewage and nonbiodegradable plastic directly affect land, drains, and water bodies.

items.label: Acid rain forming from dissolved gases

q1c2l2.q: Sort these environmental problems into Air Pollution or Land, Water & Waste problems.

q1c2l2.explain: A chemical change occurs when the composition and structure of matter change to form a completely new material.
options: It changes and forms a new material.
It stays the same, changing only its size.
It changes only its form and shape.
q1c2l2.q: What happens to the composition and structure of matter during a chemical change?

q1c2l2.explain: Heating sugar causes its components to react with the air, turning it into a dry black substance called carbon.
q1c2l2.q: When sugar is heated, it melts, bubbles, and eventually turns into what dry black substance?

q1c2l2.explain: Iron reacts with oxygen in the air to form rust, and salt water speeds up this chemical reaction.
q1c2l2.q: What substance speeds up the rusting process when iron reacts with oxygen in the air?

q1c2l2.explain: Photosynthesis is a chemical process where plants combine carbon dioxide and water into glucose (food).
q1c2l2.q: Which useful chemical change in plants combines carbon dioxide and water to create glucose?

q1c2l2.explain: Carbon monoxide is a poisonous gas that causes drowsiness and headaches, and can cause unconsciousness or death in larger amounts.
q1c2l2.q: Which toxic gas formed from burning fuel with too little oxygen causes drowsiness, headaches, or even death?

q1c2l2.explain: Acid rain forms when sulfur dioxide and nitrogen dioxide dissolve in raindrops, damaging buildings, metals, and fish.
q1c2l2.q: What forms when oxides of sulfur and nitrogen dissolve in raindrops?

q1c2l2.explain: Nonbiodegradable materials like plastic and rubber take hundreds to thousands of years to decompose, or never do.
options: They take hundreds to thousands of years to decompose.
They turn into food for plants right away.
They easily turn into paper when buried.
q1c2l2.q: Why are plastic bags and rubber considered nonbiodegradable materials?

q1c2l2.explain: Waste in dumpsites can leach toxins and methane gas, which is flammable and a potent greenhouse gas, into the soil.
q1c2l2.q: What flammable greenhouse gas can leach into the soil and air from piled-up dumpsites?

q1c2l2.explain: Burning paper creates ash and smoke. Because a new material is formed and the original paper cannot be easily recovered, it is a chemical change.
options: Because the paper only changes its size.
Because it produces ash and smoke, forming a new material.
Because the paper can easily be folded back into its original form.
Because the paper remains unchanged under heat.
q1c2l2.q: Why is burning paper classified as a chemical change rather than a physical change?

q1c2l2.explain: Making bread uses heat and chemical reactions to turn ingredients into a completely new product where individual ingredients can no longer be told apart.
options: The individual ingredients can still be easily separated after baking.
The ingredients only change their temperature.
Mixing ingredients and adding heat changes them into a new product where individual ingredients cannot be identified.
The flour only changes its shape when water is added.
q1c2l2.q: Why is making bread considered a chemical change?

q1c2l2.explain: During a physical change, only the form, size, and shape change. The composition and structure stay the same because no new material is formed.
q1c2l2.q: In a physical change, which of the following stays the same?

q1c2l2.explain: According to the lesson notes, lead particulates in polluted air can cause brain damage.
q1c2l2.q: What health issue can lead particulates in the air cause, according to the lesson?

q1c2l2.explain: Food spoilage is a chemical change where chemical reactions during decay create bad-smelling gas.
options: Physical boiling of water in the food
q1c2l2.q: What produces the bad-smelling gas when food spoils?

q1c2l2.explain: Digestion is a useful chemical change because it breaks food down into simpler forms that the body can absorb.
options: It combines carbon dioxide and water into glucose.
It turns food into nonbiodegradable material.
It breaks food down into simpler forms the body can absorb.
It prevents lead particles from entering the lungs.
q1c2l2.q: Why is digestion considered a useful chemical change in the human body?

q1c2l2.explain: The food industry uses chemical processes to extend the shelf life of canned and packed food, as well as to produce cheese and milk.
options: By turning all food into carbon monoxide
By extending the shelf life of canned and packed food
By boiling water to freeze food instantly
By mixing plastic bags into food containers
q1c2l2.q: How does the food industry use chemical changes to help food last longer?

q1c2l2.explain: When harmful chemicals leach into the soil from improperly managed dump sites, it lowers the quality of crops.
q1c2l2.q: What happens to crops when harmful chemicals from poorly managed dump sites leach into the soil?

q1c2l2.explain: Nonbiodegradable materials take a very long time to decompose. When they accumulate and clog drains, they can cause flash floods.
q1c2l2.q: What environmental problem can occur when nonbiodegradable items like plastic bags clog drains?

q1c2l2.explain: Oxides of sulfur and nitrogen cause breathing difficulty, fading paint, and damaged crops, in addition to forming acid rain.
q1c2l2.q: Besides breathing difficulties, what harm can toxic oxides of sulfur and nitrogen cause to non-living objects?

q1c2l2.explain: To help prevent pollution, the lesson recommends walking or biking for short trips, not burning garbage, and segregating waste.
options: Walking or biking for short trips
q1c2l2.q: Which of the following is recommended in the lesson to help prevent pollution?

q1c2l2.explain: Absorbing water only changes the paper towel's form or wetness without creating a new material, so it is a physical change.
options: The paper towel turns into a dry black substance.
The paper towel reacts with oxygen to form rust.
No new material is formed when water is absorbed.
Bad-smelling gas is released during absorption.
q1c2l2.q: Why is a paper towel absorbing water classified as a physical change?

q1c2l2.explain: Particulates such as dust, ash, and soot enter the air and cause breathing problems like bronchitis and asthma.
q1c2l2.q: What respiratory health issues can particulates like dust, ash, and soot cause, according to the lesson?

q1c2l2.explain: When sulfur and nitrogen oxides dissolve in raindrops to form acid rain, it destroys metals and buildings and kills fish.
options: It makes fish grow too fast.
It turns water into salt water.
q1c2l2.q: What harmful effect does acid rain have on living organisms in bodies of water, based on the notes?

q1c2l2.explain: Wood rotting is a chemical change because decay creates new materials, and the original wood cannot easily be identified or returned to its initial state.
options: A physical change, because the wood only changes shape
A chemical change, because decay breaks it down into new materials
A physical change, because the wood can easily be put back together
No change at all, because the wood stays exactly the same
q1c2l2.q: What type of change takes place when wood rots?

q1c2l2.explain: The lesson states that soaps, shampoo, toothpaste, and clothing fibers are also created through chemical processes.
options: Soaps, shampoo, toothpaste, and clothing fibers
q1c2l2.q: Besides food products like cheese and milk, which useful non-food items mentioned in the lesson are made using chemical processes?

q1c2l2.explain: According to the lesson, sewage contaminates rivers, lakes, and seashores when waste is improperly managed.
options: They evaporate completely into acid rain.
They release nitrogen oxides into the air.
q1c2l2.q: What happens to natural bodies of water like rivers, lakes, and seashores when human waste is managed poorly?

q1c2l2.explain: Alcohol evaporating is a physical change because only its physical form changes (from liquid to gas), while its composition stays the same.
options: A chemical change, because a gas with a new composition is created
A physical change, because only its form changes from liquid to gas
A chemical change, because heat destroys the alcohol
A permanent change that creates ash
q1c2l2.q: When alcohol evaporates into the air, what kind of change is happening?

q1c2l2.explain: The lesson explains that while some substances interact naturally, others need a trigger, such as heat causing sugar to caramelize.
q1c2l2.q: Some chemical changes happen naturally, but others need an outside factor to start. What does the lesson call this factor, such as heat for caramelizing sugar?

q1c2l2.explain: In a chemical change, a new material forms, so the original material's characteristics can no longer easily be identified.
options: They become much easier to see.
They can no longer easily be identified.
They stay exactly the same as before.
They double in size and weight.
q1c2l2.q: What happens to the characteristics of an original material after a chemical change occurs?

q1c2l2.explain: Inflating a tire only changes its form, size, and shape without forming a new material, so it is a physical change.
options: Because air forms a brand-new material inside the tire
Because only the tire's form, size, and shape change
Because the rubber reacts chemically with the air
Because it produces a bad-smelling gas
q1c2l2.q: Why is inflating a tire with air classified as a physical change?

q1c2l2.explain: Cooking a pancake involves heat reacting with ingredients to form a new product, making it a chemical change.
options: Because heat causes the components to react and form a new material
Because the pancake can easily be turned back into liquid milk and flour
Because only the shape of the pancake pan changes
Because no new material is formed
q1c2l2.q: When cooking a pancake, the liquid batter changes into a soft, fluffy food. Why is cooking a pancake considered a chemical change?

q1c2l2.explain: Souring milk is a chemical change because chemical reactions take place as food spoils, creating new substances.
q1c2l2.q: Milk souring is classified as a physical change because only its form changes.
q1c2l2.topic: How Chemical Change in Matter Occurs

q1c2l2.explain: Photosynthesis is a chemical process in plants that combines carbon dioxide and water into glucose.
q1c2l2.q: Photosynthesis is a useful chemical change that combines carbon dioxide and water to make glucose.
q1c2l2.topic: How Chemical Change in Matter Occurs

q1c2l2.explain: Salt water speeds up the rusting process when iron reacts with oxygen in the air.
q1c2l2.q: Salt water slows down the process of iron reacting with oxygen to form rust.
q1c2l2.topic: How Chemical Change in Matter Occurs

q1c2l2.explain: Carbon monoxide is a toxic gas created when fuel burns with an insufficient supply of oxygen.
q1c2l2.q: Carbon monoxide is a poisonous gas formed when fuel burns with too little oxygen.
q1c2l2.topic: How Chemical Change in Matter Occurs

q1c2l2.explain: Nonbiodegradable materials like plastic take hundreds to thousands of years to decompose.
q1c2l2.q: Nonbiodegradable products like plastic bottles take only a few days to decompose in nature.
q1c2l2.topic: How Chemical Change in Matter Occurs

q1c2l2.explain: Methane gas produced by decomposing waste in dumpsites is both flammable and a greenhouse gas.
q1c2l2.q: Methane gas released from waste in dump sites is flammable and acts as a greenhouse gas.
q1c2l2.topic: How Chemical Change in Matter Occurs

q1c2l2.explain: When sugar is heated, its components react with air to form a dry black substance known as carbon.
q1c2l2.q: Heating sugar causes it to melt, bubble, and turn into a dry black substance called carbon.
q1c2l2.topic: How Chemical Change in Matter Occurs

q1c2l2.explain: Acid rain forms when sulfur dioxide and nitrogen dioxide dissolve in raindrops, not carbon monoxide.
q1c2l2.q: Acid rain forms when carbon monoxide dissolves into raindrops.
q1c2l2.topic: How Chemical Change in Matter Occurs

q1c2l2.explain: Burning paper is a chemical change because the paper turns into ash and smoke, creating a new material.
q1c2l2.q: When paper burns into ash and smoke, a chemical change takes place because a new material is formed.
q1c2l2.topic: How Chemical Change in Matter Occurs

q1c2l2.explain: Cutting an apple is a physical change because only its size and shape change, while its composition remains the same.
q1c2l2.q: Cutting an apple into smaller slices is a chemical change because its composition changes.
q1c2l2.topic: How Chemical Change in Matter Occurs

notes.html:
HEOGRAPIYA

Ito ay ang pag-aaral tungkol sa DAIGDIG at sa LAHAT ng NATATAGPUAN DITO

 

Kasama rito ang pag-aaral ng:

  1. Bundok
  2. Ilog at Dagat
  3. Klima
  4. Isla
  5. Lungsod
  6. Tao

 

BAKIT MAHALAGA ANG HEOGRAPIYA?

 

Mahalaga ang heograpiya dahil:

 

  • Nalalaman natin kung saan matatagpuan ang iba't ibang lugar.
  • Naiintindihan natin ang ating kapaligiran.
  • Natututuhan nating pangalagaan ang kalikasan.
  • Nakatutulong ito kapag tayo ay naglalakbay.
  • Mas nakikilala natin ang ating bansang Pilipinas.

 

MAPA

  • Isang PALAPAD NA REPRESENTASYON ng daigdig
  • Isang guhit o larawan ng isang lugar
  • Nagtuturo ito ng EKSAKTONG KINALALAGYAN ng isang lugar

 

BAKIT GUMAGAMIT NG MAPA?

  • Para madaling makita ang direksyon (HILAGA, TIMOG, SILANGAN, KANLURAN).
  • Para malaman ang lokasyon ng isang lugar.
  • Para hindi tayo maligaw.

GLOBO

  • Isang BILOG na MODELO ng ating mundo
  • Ipinapakita nito ang TUNAY NA HUGIS ng daigdig
  • Makikita din dito ang: 7 CONTINENTS at 5 OCEANS

7 CONTINENTS:

  1. Asia
  2. Africa
  3. North America
  4. South America
  5. Antarctica
  6. Europe
  7. Australia at Oceana

 

5 OCEANS:

  1. Pacific Ocean
  2. Atlantic Ocean
  3. Indian Ocean
  4. Southern Ocean
  5. Arctic Ocean

 

BAKIT GUMAGAMIT NG GLOBO?

  • Ginagamit ito upang makita ang KABUUAN ng mundo at kung saan matatagpuan ang iba't ibang bansa

 

ANO ANG PAGKAKAIBA NG MAPA AT GLOBO?

 

MAPA

GLOBO

PATAG ang itsura

BILOG ang hugis

Maaring maliit o malaki ang lugar na ipinapakita

Tumpak na MODELO NG DAIGDIG kaya HINDI NAKIKITA ang lahat ng lugar ng sabay-sabay

Ginagamit sa paghahanap ng mga KALYE, BARANGAY at LUNGSOD

Ito ay mas angkop gamitin upang ipakita ang PAG-IKOT NG MUNDO

 

  1. TIYAK NA LOKASYON (ABSOLUTE LOCATION)
  • Ito ang EKSAKTONG KINAROROONAN ng isang lugar.
  • Tumutukoy sa eksaktong kinaroroonan ng isang lugar sa ibabaw ng daigdig. Ito ay karaniwang natutukoy gamit ang mga koordinado ng latitude at longitude na bumubuo sa grid system ng globo at mapa.

 

LONGITUDE

  • Pataas at pababa na guhit (UP AND DOWN)
  • Mga guhit mula HILAGANG POLO hanggang TIMOG POLO
  • Sinusukat nito kung gaano KALAYO ang isang lugar MULA sa PRIME MERIDIAN
  • Tumutukoy sa lokasyon sa SILANGAN o KANLURAN ng PRIME MERIDIAN

 

LATITUDE

  • Mga guhit na PAIKOT sa daigdig (RIGHT AND LEFT)
  • Sinusukat nito kung GAANO KALAYO ang isang lugar MULA SA EKWADOR (EQUATOR)
  • Tumutukoy ito sa lokasyon sa HILAGA o TIMOG ng EKWADOR
     

 

PRIME MERIDIAN

  • Ito ay may sukat na 0 DEGREE LONGITUDE
  • Ito ang PINAGMUMULAN NG ORAS sa buong mundo o tinatawag na: GREENWICH MEAN TIME (GMT) o COORDINATED UNIVERSAL TIME (UTC)

 

HALIMBAWA NG LONGITUDE AT LATITUDE:

  • May sariling latitude at longitude ang PILIPINAS kaya mas madaling makita ang EKSAKTONG LOKASYON nito ng mga piloto, mandaragat at mga gumagawa ng mapa

 

TANDAAN:

Tiyak na lokasyon = Eksakyong loksayon gamit ang LATITUDE at LONGITUDE

 

  1. RELATIBONG LOKASYON (RELATIVE LOCATION)
  • Ito ay nagsasabi kung ano ang NASA PALIGID ng isang lugar.
  • Nahahati ito sa DALAWANG PAMAMARAAN:
  1. BISINAL - mga kalapit na BANSA o LUPA
  2. INSULAR - mga nakapaligid na ANYONG TUBIG

 

LOKASYONG BISINAL

  • Pagtukoy sa LOKASYON ng isang bansa o lugar gamit ang mga kalapit nitong mga BANSA o ANYONG LUPA

 

LOKASYONG INSULAR

  • Pagtukoy sa isang lokasyong gamit ang mga nakapaligid na ANYONG TUBIG

 

HALIMBAWA NG RELATIBONG LOKASYON:

 

TAIWAN - nasa hilaga

VIETNAM - nasa kanluran

INDONESIA - nasa timog

KARAGATANG PASIPIKO - nasa silangan

 

 

 

  1. ANG LOKASYON NG PILIPINAS SA ASYA AT SA MUNDO

 

  • Ang PILIPINAS ay isang bansang matatagpuan sa TIMOG-SILANGANG ASYA (SOUTHEAST ASIA)
  • Ito ay kabilang sa kontinente ng ASYA, ang PINAKAMALAKING KONTINENTE sa mundo
  • Binubuo ang Pilipinas ng MAHIGIT 7,000 PULO, kaya ito ay tinatawag na KAPULUAN (ARCHIPELAGO)

 

ANO ANG TIMOG - SILANGANG ASYA?

  • Ito ay isang REHIYON sa kontinente ng Asya
  • Maraming bansa ang matatagpuan dito, kabilang na ang:
    1. Pilipinas
    2. Malaysia
    3. Indonesia
    4. Thailand
    5. Singapore
    6. Brunei
    7. Vietnam

 

BAKIT MAHALAGA ANG LOKASYON NG PILIPINAS?

  • Nakikipagkalakalan (TRADE) ang Pilipinas sa ibang bansa
  • MADALING MAKAPAGLAKBAY ang mga tao
  • Maraming YAMANG-DAGAT ang ating bansa
  • NAKIKIPAGKAIBIGAN at NAKIKIPAGTULUNGAN tayo sa ibang mga bansa

 

HALIMBAWA:

  • Maraming produkto ang dumarating sa Pilipinas mula sa ating mga karatig-bansa

KONSEPTO NG BANSA

 

BANSA

  • Isang lugar o teritoryo na may NANINIRAHANG GRUPO NG MGA TAO na pinamumunuan ng isang gobyerno o pamahalaan
  • Tumutukoy ito sa lawak ng:

-lupain

-katubigan

-himpapawid at kalawakan sa itaas nito

  • Tumutukoy din ito sa grupo ng mga tao na kabahagi ng IISANG KASAYSAYAN, TRADISYON, KULTURA, WIKA, LAHI at TERITORYO

 

TERITORYO

  • HANGGANAN ng nasasakupan ng isang bansa
  • Kapag LABAS na sa hangganan ay maaaring pagmamay-ari na ng IBANG BANSA o kaya ay para sa PANGKALAHATANG GAMIT gaya ng INTERNATIONAL WATERS

 

INTERNATIONAL WATERS

  • Bahagi ng karagatan kung saan MALAYANG MAKAPAGLALAYAG ang SINUMAN sa mundo

 

HALIMBAWA NG PAGLABAS SA BANSA

  • Kapag ang isang tao ay LUMABAS ng bansang kinabibilangan nya, kinakailangan niyang magpakita ng mga DOKUMENTO na PINAPAYAGAN syang pumunta sa isang bansa
  • Ito ay isang patunay na IBANG PAMAHALAAN na ang may sakop sa lugar na iyong pupuntahan

 

Unang napapansin sa mga tao sa isang bansa ay ang PANLABAS NA ANYO gaya ng:

  • Hugis ng muka
  • Kulay ng balat
  • Taas (height)

 

4 NA ELEMENTO PARA TAWAGING ISANG BANSA (Montevideo Convention):

 

  1. Teritoryo
  2. Tao
  3. Pamahalaan
  4. Soberaniya

 

ANG TERITORYO NG PILIPINAS:

  • Ang SARILING TERITORYO ay isang katangian na maaarig IPAGMALAKI ng PILIPINAS bilang isang bansa

 

PILIPINAS:

  • Nasa gawing TIMOG-SILANGAN NG ASYA
  • LOKASYON: Pagitan ng 4°at 21°  LATITUD AT 116° 127° SILANGANG LONGHTITUD
  • LAWAK NG LUPAIN: MAHIGIT 300,000 km2
  • LAWAK NG BAYBAYING DAGAT: 36,289 kilometro

 

MGA DULONG BAHAGI NG PILIPINAS:

SALIGAN NG TERITORYO NG PILIPINAS

 

  1. BATAY SA KASAYSAYAN

 

  • KASUNDUAN NG PARIS (TREATY OF PARIS)

 

  • TUMAPOS sa digmaan ng ESTADOS UNIDOS at ESPANYA na naganap noong APRIL 25 -AUGUST 12, 1898
  • NAGWAGI ang ESTADOS UNIDOS sa digmaan
  • Nilagdaan ag kasunduan ng mga kinatawan ng gobyerno ng ESTADOS UNIDOS at kaharin ng ESPANYA noong DECEMBER 10, 1898
  • Nakasaad dito na sa kasunduan na ISUSUKO NG ESPANYA ang mga bansang ito sa ESTADOS UNIDOS:

  • Dahil dito, naipasailalim ulit ang Pilipinas sa kapangyarihan ng Estados Unidos

PULO NG SPRATLY o SPRATLY ISLANDS

  1. PAGPAPAHALAGA SA MGA SALIGAN NG TERITORYO NG PILIPINAS

 

  • Ang BAWAT BAHAGI ng teritoryo ng Pilipinas ay MAHALAGA
  • Ngunit MAS MAHALAGA na mayroon ang bansa natin na MATIBAY at KONGKRETONG PATUNAY na sa PILIPINAS ang teritoryong ginagalawan ng mga mamamayan
  • Ang nasasakupan ng Pilipinas ay napasakamay ng mga Pilipino dahil may KATANGGAP-TANGGAP na dahilan AT HINDI ipinilit laman o gumamit ng puwersa o dahas upang maangkin ito

Lesson 1: Internal Components of the Computer

What is a Computer?
A computer is an electronic machine that receives information (input), follows instructions, produces results (output). 

What Can a Computer Do?
A computer can:
  • Type letters and words
  • Draw pictures
  • Play games and music
  • Search for information
  • Solve math problems

Internal Parts of a Computer

🟢 Motherboard
The motherboard is the main board inside the computer.
It connects all the computer's parts so they can work together.

🧠 CPU (Central Processing Unit)
The CPU is called the brain of the computer.
It follows instructions and processes information.

💾 Storage (Hard Disk Drive & Solid State Drive)
Storage keeps files even after the computer is turned off.
Saves pictures, videos, games, and documents permanently.
SSD is faster than HDD, while HDD usually stores more for less cost.

Imagine two school bags:
🎒 HDD = A bag with zippers and wheels. It can carry many books, but it takes longer to open.
🎒 SSD = A light backpack with no wheels. It opens quickly, is quiet, and is easier to carry.

⚡ RAM (Random Access Memory)
RAM is the computer's temporary memory.
It remembers what you're working on only while the computer is on.
If you don't save your work, it disappears when the computer shuts down.

🔌 Power Supply
The power supply gives electricity to all the computer parts.
Without it, the computer cannot work.

Easy Classroom Analogy
CPU 👩‍🏫 Teacher
RAM 🖍️ Blackboard/Whiteboard
Storage (HDD/SSD) 📓 Notebook
Power Supply ⚡ Electricity
Motherboard 🏫 Classroom that connects everything

1. Bit and Byte

Bit

Bit is short for the term "binary digit," and it is the smallest unit of data in computing. It only has a binary value of either 0 or 1.

Byte

A byte is a unit of data formed by 8 bits.

Example: 1 0 1 1 0 0 0 1  →  this string of 8 bits (1s and 0s) makes 1 byte.

2. Data Units

Storage units get bigger by multiplying by 1,024 each time — starting from the byte, all the way up to the yottabyte.

3. Data Types

Text

Letters, numbers, and symbols occupy a much smaller file size. Examples: schedule.xlsx, family.docx

Pictures

Images are stored as pixel data in formats like JPEG or PNG, where each pixel is represented by a set of bytes. Examples: palawan.jpg, bohol.png

Sounds

Sound is stored in a computer by converting sound waves into bytes, which are played through speakers or headphones. Example: Iglap.mp3


Videos

Videos combine moving pictures and sound together, so they are made up of many bytes of image data and audio data played one after another. Because of this, videos usually take up the largest file size among the data types. Example: Jackie Chan.mp4

FOUNDATIONS OF DATA MANAGEMENT

1. What is Data Management?

Data management refers to storing and saving data so we can easily access them whenever we need to. This includes making sure our data is protected from being corrupted or stolen.

 2. Data Corruption

Data corruption occurs when data becomes damaged, making it unreadable or unusable when we try to open it again.

 Possible Causes of Data Corruption

•     Power failure or sudden shutdown

•     Hardware problems

•     Improper ejection of storage devices

•     Computer viruses

 3. Two Types of Memory

Primary Memory (RAM)

RAM temporarily holds data while the computer is running. You can check how much RAM is being used through the Task Manager:

•     Step 1: Press Ctrl + Alt + Delete and select Task Manager.

•     Step 2: Click the Performance tab.

•     Step 3: Click Memory to see how much RAM your computer is using.

•     Step 4: Close programs you are not using to free up memory (RAM).

 Secondary Memory (HDD and SSD)

Secondary memory is where data is stored long-term. It saves the data even when the computer is turned off. Unnecessary files — including images, videos, audio, and documents — may be removed by the user to free up storage space.

 4. Data Organization

Whenever you save a file, remember to create folders and categories where you can store and name your files in a way that is easy to understand and find.

Example folder categories: School Work, Games, Movies, Photos, Music, TV Shows.

 5. Data Security

Protecting your data is important to keep it safe. Firewalls and Antivirus programs help in protecting your computer from harmful threats.

•     Firewall — helps block harmful traffic from reaching your computer.

•     Anti-Virus Software — detects and removes harmful viruses.

 6. Data Backup and Data Recovery

Data Backup

Data Recovery

It is important to back up your data regularly in case the original gets lost or damaged.

This is the process of getting your files back after they are lost, deleted, or corrupted.

 Practice: Sort the Files!

Sort each file into the correct folder (Audio, Photos, Video, or Homework) by looking at its filename.

QUICK RECAP

Windows File Explorer = the file manager app used to browse, create, and organize files/folders (found on the taskbar).

Mouse basics: Left Click Once = Select; Left Click Twice = Open; Right Click Once = Show Options.

Common shortcuts: Cut (Ctrl+X), Copy (Ctrl+C), Paste (Ctrl+V), Rename (F2), Delete (Backspace/Delete).

Moving files = Cut the file, open the destination folder, then Paste.

1. What is Software?

Software consists of a series of programs or instructions that tell the computer how to process the data.

2. Types of Software

System Software

Programs that manage the computer's hardware and provide a platform for running applications. They control, coordinate, and manage all hardware and software resources.

Examples: Windows, Mac OS (operating systems)

Application Software

Programs designed to help users accomplish specific tasks.

Examples: Google Chrome, Microsoft Word, Spotify, Microsoft Paint

Development Software (Programming Software)

Development software is used to design and create other software.

Examples: Notepad++, Sublime Text Editor, Visual Studio Code

How They Work Together

Hardware  →  System Software  →  Application Software

System software sits between the hardware and the applications you use, letting programs like Microsoft Word run smoothly on the computer.

3. Role of Software in Different Fields

In Healthcare

In Factories

In Education

Software helps doctors make accurate diagnoses.

Software can control robotic arms, allowing them to perform dangerous tasks safely and efficiently.

Learning Management Systems (LMS) support schools by automatically organizing courses, assignments, and grades.

4. Common Software Challenges

Software Glitches

Slow Performance

Software Bugs

A temporary, often minor, malfunction in the software's operation.

Too many applications opened can cause lagging and slow the computer's performance.

An error, flaw, or fault in the code that causes incorrect or unintended results.

Guide Questions (Review & Answer)

•     What are the things you've learned today from our lesson?

•     What are the three types of software?

•     Name one software that you use and describe its function.


QUICK RECAP

Software = programs or instructions that tell the computer how to process data.

System Software = manages hardware and runs applications (e.g. Windows, Mac OS).

Application Software = helps users accomplish specific tasks (e.g. Chrome, Word, Spotify, Paint).

Development Software = used to design and create other software (e.g. Notepad++, Sublime, VS Code).

Software plays a role in healthcare, factories, and education (e.g. LMS platforms).

Common challenges: software glitches, slow performance, and software bugs.

Makeblock vs mBlock App

Both apps work with mBot Neo, but they control it in very different ways.

 

 

Makeblock App

Uses live programming like a remote control. When you press a button, the robot moves right away.

 

 

mBlock App

Available on computer. It allows users to send a series of programs to mBot Neo using block-based programming.

✏ REMEMBER

Makeblock App = instant, live control (like a remote).

mBlock App = block-based programs sent to the robot, used on a computer.

 

Connecting mBot Neo to Your Device

  1. Select mBot Neo as your device.
  2. Press the orange Bluetooth icon to open and pair the robot with your device.
  3. Place the mobile device near mBot Neo and wait for the beep.
  4. Wait until the device makes a beep — you can now use the Makeblock App to control mBot Neo.

Parts of Drive Mode

  • Joystick — controls the movement.
  • Power indicator — shows the motor's speed.
  • Color slider — changes the LED colors at the back of the CyberPi.
  • mBot Neo Emotes — perform 6 different actions when clicked.

 

✏ REMEMBER

Drive Mode has 4 main parts: Joystick, Power indicator, Color slider, and mBot Neo Emotes.

The Joystick is for movement; the Emotes let mBot Neo react and perform actions.

📌 PART 1: ELEMENTS OF ART

1. LINE

  • A line is the distance between two points.
  • It creates movement, rhythm, and patterns.
  • Two Kinds of Lines:
    • Straight Lines — horizontal, vertical, diagonal, perpendicular, intersecting, parallel, zigzag, jogged, broken
    • Curved Lines — spiral, wavy, concave, convex (used for free-form or organic shapes)

2. SHAPE and FORM

  • A shape is formed when lines connect to enclose a space. It is 2-dimensional (flat).
  • Two Types of Shapes:
    • Organic Shapes — irregular shapes found in nature (flowers, rocks, fruits, sea creatures, stars)
    • Geometric Shapes — sharp, precise, man-made shapes (circle, square, rectangle, triangle, oval, pentagon, hexagon, octagon)
  • Forms are 3-dimensional versions of shapes (cube, sphere, cylinder, cone, pyramid, rectangular prism).

3. COLOR

  • Color creates visual interest and expresses emotions.
  • Primary Colors — red, blue, yellow (the source of all other colors)
  • Secondary Colors — made by mixing two primary colors
  • Tertiary Colors — made by mixing one primary and one secondary color

4. VALUE

  • Value is the lightness or darkness of a color.
  • Made by mixing a color with white (lighter) or black (darker).
  • Shows the transition of color from light to dark.

5. TEXTURE

  • Texture is how a surface feels or looks — smooth, rough, soft, or hard.

6. SPACE

  • Space refers to the area around, between, and within parts of an artwork.

📌 PART 2: PRINCIPLE OF DESIGN — BALANCE

  • Balance is how visual weight is spread out in an artwork.
  • It creates stability, harmony, and comfort for the viewer.

📌 PART 3: THE ART OF PAPERCUTTING

What is Paper Cutting?

Paper cutting is the craft of making intricate designs by carefully cutting sheets of paper or parchment using scissors, knives, or scalpels.

Borlas de Pastillas (Pabalat)

  • A traditional Filipino paper-cutting art used to wrap pastillas de leche (milk candy).
  • Originates from San Miguel, Bulacan.
  • Artisans hand-cut Japanese paper (papel de hapon) into floral, rural, or festive designs.
  • Purpose: keeps hands from getting sticky while eating the sweet, and adds beauty to the treat.

Materials Needed for Paper Cutting

  • Colored paper
  • Scissors or cutter/knife
  • Cutting mat
  • Pencil (for tracing the design first)
  • Glue (optional, for assembling)

📍 About Bohol

•     Bohol is a province in Central Visayas, Philippines.

•     It is known for its rich culture and traditions.

•     Music is an important part of Boholano life.

🎵 What is a Lullaby?

A lullaby is a gentle song sung to babies or young children to:

•     Help them sleep

•     Comfort them

•     Calm them

•     Show love and care

🌙 What are Boholano Lullabies?

Boholano lullabies are gentle songs from the province of Bohol, sung by families to help babies and young children fall asleep.

•     “Boholano” — means someone or something from Bohol, an island province in the Philippines.

•     “Lullaby” — a slow, gentle song sung to help a baby or young child fall asleep.

✨ Characteristics of Boholano Lullabies

Boholano lullabies usually have:

•     Soft and gentle melody

•     Slow tempo

•     Simple lyrics

•     Calm and peaceful mood

•     Loving message

💤 Tingkatulog: A Boholano Lullaby

Tingkatulog is a folk lullaby song from Bohol, Philippines, that means “sleeping time.” It is a soft, slow song that comforts a sleepy child by promising that the mother will return soon.

Lyrics of Tingkatulog

Pinalangga, mari ka, katulog na

Katulog, pahulay, aron modaku

Ang imong higdaan

Andam na ug katulog na

Hangtud si Mama mobalik

Sa ka buntagon.

•     The degree of loudness and softness of sound.

Dialogue and Action

Dance is connected to the quality of how the dancer moves. The energy of movement can be used to depict the emotion and mood as well.

notes.name: Ang Lihim sa Laptop ni Lolo Luis
notes.text:
Magandang araw sa inyong lahat! May itatanong po ako sa inyo... Nakakita na ba kayo ng robot na nagsasalita ng 'Po' at 'Opo'?

Ganito ang kuwento ng kaibigan kong si Lito. Isang hapon, problemadong-problemado siya dahil sa kanyang takdang-aralin sa kasaysayan ng Pilipinas. Ang kapal ng mga aklat at ang lala-lim ng mga salita! Tumingin siya sa orasan... Tiktak, tiktak! Ang bilis ng oras!

Dahil gabi na, pinahiram siya ng kanyang Lolo Luis ng isang makabagong laptop.

Lolo Luis: Gamitin mo ito, apo. May AI o Artificial Intelligence iyan. Matalino iyan!

Nang buksan ni Lito ang computer... Bzzzt... Whoosh! Isang boses-robot ang narinig niya!

AI Assistant: Magandang gabi, Lito. Ako ang iyong AI Assistant. Ano ang maaari kong isaliksik para sa iyo ngayon?

Nanlaki ang mga mata ni Lito!

Lito: Hala! Marunong ka po mag-Filipino?

AI Assistant: Siyempre naman, Lito. Ang Wikang Filipino ay tulay sa yaman ng impormasyon. Kapag tinanong mo ako sa Filipino, isasaliksik ko ang sagot sa pinakamabilis na paraan.

Agad na nag-type si Lito:

Lito: Ano ang mga sikat na tradisyon sa Pilipinas?

Zing! Zing! Sa isang kurap lang, lumabas sa screen ang kuwento ng Bayanihan at mga makukulay na kapistahan. Lahat ay nakasulat sa malinaw at madaling maunawaang Wikang Filipino! Dahil sa AI, mabilis na natapos ni Lito ang kanyang proyekto.

Doon naintindihan ni Lito ang tunay na kahulugan ng ating tema ngayon. Ang AI o teknolohiya ay hindi kaaway ng ating wika, at hindi rin ito ginawa para tayo ay maging tamad. Ito ay isang makabagong kasangkapan. Kapag ginamit natin ito sa tamang paraan gamit ang ating sariling wika, mas madali nating matutuklasan ang yaman ng kaalaman ng ating bansa.

Kaya mga kamag-aral, sa tulong ng teknolohiya at pagmamahal sa sariling wika, magsaliksik tayo at mag-aral nang mabuti!

Kami po si George at Charlie nag-iiwan sa inyo ng hamon: Gamitin ang teknolohiya, mahalin ang Wikang Filipino! Maraming salamat po at mabuhay tayong lahat!

notes.html:
Overview

Building a successful business rarely comes down to just one strength — it's really a mix of many qualities. Some days call for hard work and discipline to keep things running. Other days call for resourcefulness and creativity to figure out a solution nobody's tried yet. Confidence and decisiveness help push an idea forward, while honesty and cooperation are what keep customers and partners coming back. And when things don't go as planned, it's perseverance and optimism that keep an entrepreneur moving instead of giving up.

The good news is, these characteristics aren't something only "born entrepreneurs" have — they're things any of us can practice and grow, whether in business, in school, or simply in how we treat the people around us.

The 10 Qualities at a Glance

Quality

What It Means

Hard Work

Willingness to put in effort and time to accomplish tasks.

Resourcefulness

Ability to find ways to solve problems using available materials or ideas.

Confidence

Belief in one's own abilities and decisions.

Honesty

Being truthful and fair in dealings with customers and partners.

Creativity

Ability to think of new ideas or improve existing ones.

Perseverance

Continuing to try despite challenges, setbacks, or failures.

Discipline

Ability to control oneself and follow a planned routine or set of rules.

Cooperation

Willingness to work well with others toward a common goal.

Decisiveness

Ability to make timely and well-thought-out decisions.

Optimism

Staying hopeful and positive, even when facing setbacks.

A Closer Look at Each Quality

1. HARD WORK

•     Willingness to put in effort and time to accomplish tasks.

•     Businesses require consistent effort to grow and succeed.

Sample Scenarios:

1.      Waking up early every day to prepare ingredients for a food stall.

2.      Continuing to sell products even on rainy days.

3.      Staying late to finish orders for customers.

4.      Practicing a skill repeatedly to improve product quality (e.g., baking, sewing).

5.      Doing extra tasks like cleaning the stall or fixing displays without being told.

2. RESOURCEFULNESS

•     Ability to find ways to solve problems using available materials or ideas.

•     Helps entrepreneurs overcome challenges like limited budget or supplies.

Sample Scenarios:

1.      Using recycled materials for product packaging.

2.      Finding a cheaper supplier when prices go up.

3.      Repurposing leftover cloth to make small accessories.

4.      Using social media instead of paid ads to promote a product.

5.      Asking family members to help when there's no budget to hire workers.

3. CONFIDENCE

•     Belief in one's own abilities and decisions.

•     Helps entrepreneurs take initiative and make sound decisions.

Sample Scenarios:

1.      Approaching new customers to introduce a product.

2.      Presenting a business idea to family or friends.

3.      Setting a fair price for a product without doubting oneself.

4.      Speaking clearly and confidently when explaining a product's benefits.

5.      Trying a new business idea despite the fear of failing.

4. HONESTY

•     Being truthful and fair in dealings with customers and partners.

•     Builds trust, which keeps customers coming back.

Sample Scenarios:

1.      Giving the correct change to a customer.

2.      Telling a customer the true price of a product, even if it's a small amount.

3.      Admitting a mistake, like giving the wrong item, and fixing it right away.

4.      Not overpricing products just to earn more.

5.      Being truthful about a product's quality or ingredients.

5. CREATIVITY

•     Ability to think of new ideas or improve existing ones.

•     Helps a business stand out and adapt to customer needs.

Sample Scenarios:

1.      Designing a unique logo or packaging for a product.

2.      Coming up with a new flavor or variation of a food item.

3.      Thinking of a catchy name for a business.

4.      Creating fun ways to display products to attract customers.

5.      Finding a new way to solve a common customer complaint.

6. PERSEVERANCE

•     Continuing to try despite challenges, setbacks, or failures.

•     Helps entrepreneurs push through difficulties instead of giving up.

Sample Scenarios:

1.      Trying again after a product doesn't sell well the first time.

2.      Continuing a business even after losing some capital.

3.      Practicing a skill multiple times until it improves.

4.      Staying motivated even when sales are slow for a few days.

5.      Finding new customers after losing a regular one.

7. DISCIPLINE

•     Ability to control oneself and follow a planned routine or set of rules.

•     Helps entrepreneurs manage time, money, and tasks responsibly.

Sample Scenarios:

1.      Setting a fixed time to open and close a stall every day.

2.      Saving part of the profit instead of spending it all right away.

3.      Following a schedule for preparing and selling products.

4.      Keeping track of expenses and earnings regularly.

5.      Avoiding impulsive purchases that are not needed for the business.

8. COOPERATION

•     Willingness to work well with others toward a common goal.

•     Helps build strong relationships with partners, helpers, and customers.

Sample Scenarios:

1.      Working with family members to prepare products for selling.

2.      Sharing tasks fairly with a business partner.

3.      Listening to suggestions from customers to improve a product.

4.      Helping a co-seller when they are short-staffed.

5.      Coordinating with suppliers to ensure materials arrive on time.

9. DECISIVENESS

•     Ability to make timely and well-thought-out decisions.

•     Helps entrepreneurs respond quickly to problems and opportunities.

Sample Scenarios:

1.      Deciding quickly which product to prioritize when supplies are limited.

2.      Choosing the best supplier after comparing prices.

3.      Deciding to stop selling a product that isn't popular.

4.      Setting a price quickly based on cost and demand.

5.      Choosing a good selling location after considering foot traffic.

10. OPTIMISM

•     Staying hopeful and positive, even when facing setbacks.

•     Helps entrepreneurs keep going and see mistakes as lessons rather than failures.

Sample Scenarios:

1.      Staying hopeful about sales improving after a slow week.

2.      Seeing a mistake as a lesson rather than a failure.

3.      Believing a new product idea will eventually succeed.

4.      Encouraging a business partner during a difficult time.

5.      Focusing on what went well even after a bad sales day.

Vocabulary

Term

What It Means

Entrepreneur

A person who starts, organizes, and manages a business, taking on financial risk to do so.

Characteristic

A quality or trait that helps describe a person's behavior or personality.

Capital

Money or resources used to start or run a business.

Initiative

The ability to act on one's own, without needing to be told what to do.

Setback

A problem or difficulty that slows down or interrupts progress.

Foot traffic

The number of people walking past or visiting a place, such as a store location.

Why It Matters

Generalization

•     Why is it important for you to know your own personal characteristics before starting a business?

•     How can practicing good personal qualities today help you become a better entrepreneur or worker in the future?

1. What Is a Collective Noun?

A collective noun is a word that names a group of people, animals, or things as ONE single unit — even though the group is made up of many members.

  Remember: one word can stand for a whole group!

2. Common Collective Nouns

Groups of Animals

Word

Example

flock

a flock of birds / sheep

herd

a herd of cattle / elephants

pack

a pack of wolves / dogs

pride

a pride of lions

school

a school of fish

pod

a pod of whales / dolphins

swarm

a swarm of bees

murder

a murder of crows

gaggle

a gaggle of geese

litter

a litter of puppies

Groups of Things

Word

Example

bunch

a bunch of grapes / keys

fleet

a fleet of ships / cars

bundle

a bundle of sticks

stack

a stack of books

deck

a deck of cards

set

a set of tools

cluster

a cluster of stars

array

an array of choices

3. Subject-Verb Agreement with Collective Nouns

A collective noun can take EITHER a singular or plural verb, depending on whether the group is acting as one unit or as separate individuals.

Singular Verb — Group Acts as ONE Unit

Use this when the group is functioning together, as a whole.

•      The team is playing well this season.

•      The family lives in a small house.

•      The committee has approved the budget.

•      The jury has reached its verdict.

Plural Verb — Members Act INDIVIDUALLY

Use this when you're emphasizing the individuals within the group doing different things.

•      The team are arguing among themselves.

•      The committee disagree about the proposal.

•      The staff have different opinions.

4. Special Collective Nouns — Always Plural

Some collective nouns look singular, but they ALWAYS take a plural verb. There is no singular option for these words.

•      police, people, cattle

•      clergy, poultry, vermin

  Example: The police are investigating the case. (never “is”)

5. Quick Recap

•      Collective noun: one word for a group (people, animals, or things).

•      Singular verb: group acts together as one whole.

•      Plural verb: members of the group act as individuals.

•      Always plural: police, people, cattle, clergy, poultry, vermin.

Overview

Businesses can be classified into three major types:

•     Manufacturing

•     Services

•     Retailing

1. Manufacturing

What is it?

•     Transforms raw materials into finished products using machines, labor, and processes.

•     Produces goods like cars, food products, and clothing for daily use.

•     Creates jobs and supports industries that supply materials and services.

Examples

○    Food manufacturing – bread, canned goods, noodles, biscuits

○    Clothing manufacturing – shirts, pants, uniforms, shoes

○    Furniture manufacturing – tables, chairs, cabinets

○    Car and vehicle manufacturing – cars, motorcycles, jeepneys

○    Electronics manufacturing – cellphones, radios, televisions

○    Paper products manufacturing – notebooks, books, cartons

2. Services

What is it?

•     Provides intangible products such as skills, help, or expertise instead of physical goods.

•     Focuses on human effort and knowledge to meet people's needs.

•     Helps make daily life easier, safer, and more convenient.

Examples

○    Education – schools, teachers, tutors

○    Healthcare – hospitals, clinics, doctors, nurses

○    Banking – banks, ATMs, financial services

○    IT services – computer repair, internet services, software support

○    Transportation – drivers, delivery services, airlines

3. Retailing

What is it?

•     Involves selling goods directly to consumers for personal or household use.

•     Connects manufacturers and customers through physical stores or online platforms.

•     Makes products accessible and convenient to buy.

Examples

○    Supermarkets and grocery stores

○    Clothing and shoe stores

○    Sari-sari stores

○    Bookstores and school supply shops

○    Online stores / e-commerce platforms

Comparison at a Glance

 

Manufacturing = makes

Service = helps/does

Retailing = sells

What it does

Turns raw materials into finished products using machines, labor, and processes

Provides intangible help, skills, or expertise instead of physical goods

Sells goods directly to consumers for personal or household use

Main output

Physical goods (cars, food, clothing)

Human effort and knowledge that meets people's needs

Products made accessible and convenient to buy

Examples

Bread and canned goods, clothing, furniture, vehicles, electronics, paper products

Schools, hospitals, banks, IT services, transportation

Supermarkets, clothing stores, sari-sari stores, bookstores, online stores

Vocabulary

Term

What It Means

Business

An activity where people make, sell, or provide something to earn a living.

Manufacturing

Turning raw materials into finished products using machines, labor, and processes.

Raw materials

Basic materials used to make a finished product.

Service

An intangible product such as skill, help, or expertise given to meet people's needs.

Intangible

Something that cannot be touched or held, unlike a physical good.

Retailing

Selling goods directly to consumers for personal or household use.

Consumer

A person who buys and uses goods or services.

E-commerce

Buying and selling of goods through online platforms.

 Why It Matters

Generalization

•     What are the three types of businesses, and how are they different from each other?

•     How do businesses in your community help your family and the people around you?

1. What Are Physical Properties?

A physical property is anything about matter you can OBSERVE or MEASURE without turning it into a different substance. Physical properties come in two kinds:

A. Extensive properties — depend on the AMOUNT of matter. Less matter = smaller quantity.

B. Intensive properties — depend on the KIND of matter, not the amount. Same stuff = same property, big or small piece.

 

2. Extensive vs. Intensive — At a Glance

 

EXTENSIVE PROPERTY

INTENSIVE PROPERTY

Depends on

Amount of matter

Kind of matter

Changes if amount changes?

Yes — smaller amount, smaller value

No — stays the same

Example

A 10-kg box has more matter than a 4-kg box

Color, texture, and hardness of paper stay the same whether the sheet is big or small

 

3. Extensive Properties in Detail

•      Mass — the measure of the amount of matter

•      Volume — the amount of space matter takes up

•      Size / Length — small amount of matter = small size or length

•      Weight — the measure of gravitational pull on an object — bigger mass = bigger weight

•      Energy — greater mass = greater energy

 

4. Intensive Properties in Detail

•      Color, Texture, Hardness — look, feel, and firmness of a material — don't change with size

•      Density — the ratio of mass to volume — same for a material no matter the size of the sample

Pure water's density is 1 g/cm³ (1,000 kg/m³) — densest at 4°C, least dense at 0°C.

D = m / V

D = density (g/cm³)   ·   m = mass (g)   ·   V = volume (cm³)

Float or sink? Density < 1.0 g/cm³ → FLOATS on water.  Density > 1.0 g/cm³ → SINKS.

 

5. Vocabulary Quick List

TERM

MEANING

Physical Property

Can be observed/measured without changing the substance into another substance

Extensive Property

Depends on the amount of matter

Intensive Property

Depends on the kind of matter, same regardless of amount

Mass

The measure of the amount of matter

Volume

The amount of space matter occupies

Weight

The measure of gravitational pull on an object

Density

The ratio of mass to volume (D = m/V)

 

6. Try It Yourself

✏ REMEMBER

•      EP depends on AMOUNT: mass, volume, size, length, weight, energy

•      IP depends on KIND only: color, texture, hardness, density

•      D = m/V, in g/cm³

•      Water density = 1 g/cm³ → below it floats, above it sinks

A. Write EP if extensive property or IP if intensive property:

1. lustrous metal ring  _______

2. volume of an inflated balloon  _______

3. mass of the onion sold in the market  _______

4. hardness of the concrete wall  _______

5. temperature of the room  _______

6. length of eggplant  _______

7. aroma of the brewed coffee  _______

8. melting ice cream  _______

9. crumpled aluminum sheet  _______

10. slippery floor  _______

B. Cite three examples of extensive properties and discuss each briefly.

1. What Is a Chemical Property?

A chemical property tells us how a substance behaves when it reacts with another substance. Unlike physical properties (color, size, texture), you cannot see a chemical property just by looking — you only see it when a chemical reaction happens.

PHYSICAL PROPERTY

CHEMICAL PROPERTY

Seen or measured WITHOUT changing the substance

Seen ONLY when the substance reacts / changes into something new

Example: color, shape, mass, volume

Example: burning, rusting, decaying

2. Chemical Reaction

●     Chemical reaction — Combining two or more substances to make a new one.

●     Reactants — The starting materials.

●     Products — The new substance(s) formed.

Example: When you light a candle, the wax and oxygen (reactants) react to form heat, light, water vapor, and carbon dioxide (products).

3. Three Common Chemical Properties

A. Reacting with Other Materials

A substance shows a chemical reaction when it combines with another material to form a new substance. Lighting a candle is a simple example — the flame starts a chemical reaction.

B. Flammability & Combustibility

●     Flammability — how easily a substance catches fire / ignites.

●     Combustibility — how easily a substance burns.

A burning matchstick shows both properties — it ignites easily (flammable) and burns easily (combustible).

C. Biodegradability

●     Biodegradable — materials that decay/decompose with the help of decomposers (worms, fungi, bacteria). Examples: fruit peels, leaves, paper, wood.

●     Nonbiodegradable — materials that CANNOT be broken down by any chemical reaction. Examples: plastic, glass, styrofoam.

Signs that something is decaying: foul odor, mold, change in color/shape, worms, and bubbling. Heat, water, and microorganisms speed up decay — that's why we refrigerate leftover food to slow spoilage.

4. Chemical Safety at Home

●     Choose safe products, especially around children.

●     Store harmful chemicals in a locked cabinet, away from heat and flammable items.

●     Wash cleaning cloths before reusing or throwing them away.

●     Keep chemicals in their original boxes/bottles so they're easy to identify.

●     Check containers regularly for damage or leaks.

5. Vocabulary Quick List

Term

Meaning

Chemical property

How a substance behaves in a chemical reaction

Chemical reaction

When two or more substances combine to form new substance(s)

Reactant

The starting material(s) in a reaction

Product

The new material(s) formed after a reaction

Flammability

How easily a material ignites

Combustibility

How easily a material burns

Biodegradable

Can decay with the help of decomposers

Nonbiodegradable

Cannot be broken down by any reaction

Decomposers

Living things that break down dead matter (worms, fungi, bacteria)

6. Remember!

✏ REMEMBER

●     Chemical properties can only be observed through a chemical reaction — not just by looking.

●     Burning = a substance reacts with air, releasing heat and light.

●     Decaying = a biodegradable substance reacts with microorganisms, changing its color, smell, and nutrients.

WINDOWS FILE EXPLORER AND FILE HANDLING

1. What is a Windows File Explorer?

Microsoft Windows File Explorer is a file manager application with a graphical user interface. It helps users manage files fast and efficiently. It is typically located at the taskbar.

 2. Use of Computer Mouse

Selecting

Opening Files

Show Options

Left Click Once

Left Click Twice

Right Click Once

 2. Common Tools in Windows Explorer

Cut

Copy

Paste

Ctrl + X

Ctrl + C

Ctrl + V

 

•     Rename — press F2

•     Delete — press Backspace or Delete

 4. Creating a Folder Using Windows File Explorer

Go to the location where you want to create the folder. Example: Desktop Folder.

First Method

•     In the Home tab, select the "New Folder" button.

Second Method

•     Right-click in an empty space and select "New" then "Folder".

Type the name for your newly created folder and press "Enter".

 5. Downloading Files

Most files on the internet — such as images, audio, videos, documents, and more — can be downloaded. Here are some common ways to download files from the internet.

 Downloading Pictures from Google

•     Open your web browser and go to google.com.

•     Type what you want to search in the search bar and click "Images".

•     Choose a picture you like, right-click on it, and choose "Save image as...".

•     Pick a folder, rename the file, and click "Save".

Note: By default, saved images are stored in the "Downloads" folder.

 6. Renaming Files/Folders

•     Find the folder/file that you want to rename and click it.

•     In the Home tab, look into the Organize group and select "Rename" (or right-click and choose "Rename").

•     Type a clear and concise filename/folder name.

 6. Moving Files/Folders

•     Find the file that you need to move and right-click it to open the file options.

•     Select "Cut" — this will turn the file/folder a faded color, showing it is ready to be moved.

•     Locate and open the folder where you want to move the file.

•     Go to the Home tab, and in the Clipboard group, select "Paste" to move the file into the folder.

QUICK RECAP

Windows File Explorer = the file manager app used to browse, create, and organize files/folders (found on the taskbar).

Mouse basics: Left Click Once = Select; Left Click Twice = Open; Right Click Once = Show Options.

Common shortcuts: Cut (Ctrl+X), Copy (Ctrl+C), Paste (Ctrl+V), Rename (F2), Delete (Backspace/Delete).

Moving files = Cut the file, open the destination folder, then Paste.

notes.html:
Scientists and their inventions

  • Maria Ylagan Orosa — Filipino chemist (food technology) — invented Soyalac and darak (a vitamin B-1 rice biscuit that prevents beriberi) and popularized banana ketchup
  • Dr. Fe V. Del Mundo — Filipino biologist (medicine) — invented a bamboo incubator for rural areas without electricity, after the war
  • Ramon C. Barba — Filipino botanist/horticulturist — found how to make mangoes flower out of season using potassium nitrate, and gave up a patent so farmers could use it for free
  • Engr. Diosdado Banatao — Filipino physicist/inventor (computer technology) — designed the first single-chip 16-bit microprocessor calculator, then IBM's first system logic chip set — the first Windows graphics accelerator chip for PCs
  • Charles Robert Darwin — British naturalist & biologist — developed the theory of evolution by natural selection; published On the Origin of Species
  • Stephen W. Hawking — British theoretical physicist & cosmologist — lived with ALS from a young age; an expert on black holes who worked to unify quantum mechanics with general relativity; wrote A Brief History of Time
  • Karl Benz — German engineer & inventor (automotive engineering) — built the Benz Patent-Motorwagen in 1885, widely regarded as the first practical automobile powered by an internal combustion engine
  • Henry Ford — American industrialist & founder of Ford Motor Company — didn't invent the automobile, but revolutionized manufacturing with the moving assembly line, making cars affordable for ordinary people
  • Alexander Graham Bell — Scottish-born inventor & scientist (telecommunications) — credited with inventing and patenting the first practical telephone in 1876

A synonym is a word that means almost the same thing as another word — like happy and glad, or big and large.
An antonym is a word that means the opposite of another word — like hot and cold, or fast and slow.
Learning synonyms helps writers avoid repeating the same word again and again, making their writing more interesting.
Learning antonyms helps readers understand contrast — like comparing two very different characters or ideas.
Context clues in a sentence can help you figure out whether a new word is a synonym or antonym of a word you already know.
Verb - word that expresses action
Kind of Verbs
Action verbs tell what a person, animal, or thing does.
Examples:
sleep, jump, eat, write, talk, sing, dance
Sentence: Maria sings beautifully. ➡️ Sings is the action verb because it tells what Maria does.
Linking verbs connect the subject to information that describes it. They do not show action.
Examples:
am, is, are, was, become, seem
Sentence: The sky is blue. ➡️ Is links the subject sky to the word blue.
Helping verbs work with the main verb to tell when an action happens or how it happens.
Examples:
am, is, are, was, were, have, has, will
Sentence: She is dancing. ➡️ Is is the helping verb, and dancing is the main verb.

notes.html:
• A suffix is a word part added to the end of a word that can change its meaning or its part of speech.
  • -able and -ible mean "able to be" — like washable (able to be washed) or flexible (able to bend).
  • -ful means "full of" — like joyful (full of joy) — while -less means "without" — like fearless (without fear).
  • -ion turns a verb into a noun — like celebrate becomes celebration.
  • -er and -or often mean "a person who does something" — like teacher and actor.
  • -ly usually turns an adjective into an adverb — like quick becomes quickly — and -ness turns an adjective into a noun, like kind becomes kindness.

• Subject-verb agreement means the verb in a sentence must match the subject in number — singular subjects need singular verbs, and plural subjects need plural verbs.
  • A count noun can be counted and has a plural form — like one book, two books.
  • A mass noun (also called a non-count noun) cannot be counted individually — like rice, water, or information — and is usually treated as singular, so it takes a singular verb ("The rice is cooking.").
  • A collective noun names a group of people or things acting as one unit — like team, family, or class — and it usually takes a singular verb because the group acts together ("The team is practicing.").

e_q1c2l3.title: Subject-Verb Agreement - Mass and Count Nouns

notes.html:
The rule for subject-verb agreement is the same whether the noun is abstract or concrete: the verb must agree with the number of the subject (singular or plural), not with the type of noun. 

1. Abstract Nouns

Abstract nouns name ideas, feelings, qualities, or states (e.g., love, happiness, honesty, courage). 

Examples:

  • Love is important.
  • Honesty makes a person trustworthy.
  • Happiness comes from within.

Since these subjects are singular, they take singular verbs (is, makes, comes).

Plural abstract nouns:

  • Ideas are powerful.
  • Feelings change over time.

2. Concrete Nouns

Concrete nouns name things that can be perceived by the senses (e.g., book, dog, table, flower). 

Examples:

  • The book is on the table.
  • The dog barks loudly.
  • The flowers smell sweet.

A singular concrete noun takes a singular verb, while a plural concrete noun takes a plural verb.

Quick Comparison

Subject (Noun)TypeVerbCorrect Sentence
honestyAbstract (singular)isHonesty is the best policy.
courageAbstract (singular)helpsCourage helps people succeed.
ideasAbstract (plural)areIdeas are valuable.
chairConcrete (singular)isThe chair is broken.
dogConcrete (singular)runsThe dog runs fast.
booksConcrete (plural)areThe books are new.

Key Rule

✅ Singular noun = singular verb
✅ Plural noun = plural verb

The fact that a noun is abstract or concrete does not change subject-verb agreement. Only whether the noun is singular or plural matters.

e_q1c2l4.title: Subject-Verb Agreement - Abstract and Concrete Nouns
